82478.e: The fuse in the fuse box breaks the circuit when there is danger. That way it protects against fires.
82478.m: The fuse protects the house from too much current.

82479.q: Where in nature are there huge electric sparks?
82479.e: Lightning is a gigantic electric spark between a cloud and the ground. That is why you look for shelter in a building during a thunderstorm.
82479.m: Lightning is a huge electric spark.

82480.q: Two little bulbs are connected one after the other to the same battery. What happens if you unscrew one?
82480.e: With bulbs connected one after the other, there is only one path for the current. If one bulb is missing, the whole circuit is broken.
82480.m: In a series circuit, all the bulbs go out together.

82481.q: What does a yellow warning triangle with a black lightning bolt mean?
82481.e: This sign hangs, for example, on electricity boxes and transformer stations. It warns of dangerous electrical voltage.
82481.m: The lightning sign warns of electricity.

82482.q: What happens when you press the light switch?
a: The lamp goes on or off
82482.e: The switch lets the current flow to the lamp or stops it. That is why the light goes on or off.
82482.m: You turn the light on and off with the light switch.

82483.q: What is a switch that lets you make the light brighter and dimmer called?
82483.e: With a dimmer you can smoothly change the brightness of a lamp. That way you can match the light to the mood.
82483.m: You adjust the brightness with a dimmer.

82484.q: What is a device that switches the light on by itself when someone moves called?
82484.e: A motion sensor senses when someone comes near and then switches the light on. You often find one by front doors.
82484.m: A motion sensor switches on the light when there is movement.

82485.q: Why does the light in the stairwell often go off by itself after a few minutes?
a: So the lamp can cool down
82485.e: A timer switch turns the light off after a set time. That way it does not stay on for hours when nobody is there.
82485.m: A timer switch helps save electricity.

82486.q: Why do some light switches glow faintly in the dark?
a: So you can find them more easily
82486.e: A tiny lamp in the switch shows where it is in a dark room. So you do not have to feel along the wall for long.
82486.m: You can find glowing switches even in the dark.

82487.q: Can you switch the same lamp on and off with two switches at different ends of a corridor?
82487.e: With two-way switching you can switch the light at both ends of a corridor or staircase. That is very handy.
82487.m: With two switches you can switch a lamp from two places.

82488.q: What is a switch that only gives current as long as you press it, for example on a doorbell, called?
82488.e: A push button springs back as soon as you let go. That is why the doorbell only rings as long as you press it.
82488.m: A push button only works while you press it.

82489.q: What do you do if wires are sticking out of a light switch?
a: Do not touch them and fetch an adult
Clean them with a wet cloth
82489.e: Loose wires can be live. That is why you do not touch them and get help straight away.

82490.q: Why is an electric cable covered in plastic on the outside?
a: The plastic protects against electric shocks
82490.e: Inside are wires that the current flows through. The plastic covering stops you from touching the current.
82490.m: The covering of a cable protects you from electricity.

82491.q: What do you do with a device whose cable is damaged?
82491.e: With a damaged cable you can get an electric shock. The device must be repaired or replaced.
82491.m: Do not use devices with a broken cable.

82492.q: Why should you not lay electric cables under a carpet or trap them in doors?
a: They can get damaged and overheat
82492.e: A trapped cable can break inside. Then it can get hot and even start a fire.
82492.m: Cables need room and must not be trapped.

82493.q: What are the tall structures that carry power lines across the country called?
82493.e: Electricity pylons hold the lines high above the ground. That way electricity can get from the power station to the towns.
82493.m: Pylons carry power lines across the country.

82494.q: Why do you never fly a kite near power lines?
a: There is a deadly danger from electricity
The kite flies too fast there
The line takes away the wind
The birds get in the way there
82494.e: If the kite gets caught in a line, the current can flow down the string to the person. That can kill.
82494.m: Fly kites far away from power lines.

82495.q: What makes climbing onto a parked railway carriage deadly dangerous?
82495.e: The railway’s overhead line carries 15,000 volts. The current can jump across even if you only come close to the line.
82495.m: Keep away from railway carriages and overhead lines.

82496.q: What is a cable that lets a device stand further away from the socket called?
82496.e: An extension lead has a plug at one end and a socket at the other. That way the electricity reaches further.
82496.m: An extension lead takes the electricity further.

82497.q: Why should you unroll a cable reel completely before plugging in a powerful device?
82497.e: A rolled-up cable cannot give off its heat. With powerful devices it can overheat.
82497.m: Always unroll a cable reel completely.

82498.q: Where do you often see solar cells on houses?
82498.e: On the roof, the solar cells get a lot of sunlight. They do not bother anyone there either.
82498.m: Solar cells belong in a sunny spot.

82499.q: What do you call lots of solar cells sitting together on one panel?
82499.e: A single solar cell only supplies a little electricity. That is why many are joined together to make a solar module.
82499.m: Lots of solar cells make a solar module.

82500.q: When does a solar cell produce the most electricity?
a: At midday on a sunny day
In the middle of the night
82500.e: The more sunlight falls on the cell, the more electricity it produces. At midday the Sun is at its highest.
82500.m: Lots of sun means lots of solar power.

82501.q: Which small device often has a tiny solar cell?
82501.e: Some calculators need so little electricity that a small solar cell is enough. They then work without a battery.

82502.q: What colour are solar cells usually?
82502.e: Dark surfaces absorb a lot of light. That is why solar cells are usually dark blue or black.
82502.m: Solar cells are dark so they absorb a lot of light.

82503.q: On which mountain in the Bernese Jura has a well-known solar power station stood since 1992?
82503.e: The Mont-Soleil solar power station was one of the first large solar plants in Switzerland. The name “Soleil” means sun in French.
82503.m: On Mont-Soleil, electricity is made from the sun.

82504.q: Which direction is best for solar cells to face in Switzerland?
82504.e: Here, the Sun is in the south at midday. That is why south-facing solar cells get the most light.
82504.m: In Switzerland, solar cells work best facing south.

82505.q: What happens to solar power from the roof that the family does not need right now?
a: It flows into the grid or into a battery
It turns into heat in the roof
82505.e: Surplus electricity can flow into the public grid and be used by others. Or it can be stored in a battery in the house.
82505.m: Surplus solar power is shared or stored.

82506.q: What makes a wind turbine turn?
82506.e: The wind pushes against the blades and turns them. A generator inside turns this into electricity.
82506.m: A wind turbine makes electricity from wind.

82507.q: How many blades do most large wind turbines have?
82507.e: Almost all modern large wind turbines have three rotor blades. That way they turn calmly and evenly.
82507.m: Large wind turbines usually have three blades.

82508.q: Where is the largest wind farm in Switzerland?
a: On Mont-Crosin in the Bernese Jura
On the shore of Lake Geneva
82508.e: The first wind turbines were built on Mont-Crosin in 1996. Today 16 turbines turn there; it is the largest wind farm in Switzerland.
82508.m: Mont-Crosin is Switzerland’s best-known wind farm.

82509.q: Why are wind turbines often put on hills and ridges?
a: The wind blows more strongly there
82509.e: High up and on open ridges, the wind blows more strongly and steadily. That way the wind turbines produce more electricity.
82509.m: Wind turbines need places with lots of wind.

82510.q: What were windmills mainly used for in the past?
82510.e: The sails of the windmill turned heavy millstones. These were used to grind grain into flour.
82510.m: Windmills used to grind grain into flour.

82511.q: Why are wind turbines stopped in a very violent storm?
a: So they do not get damaged
So they can sleep at night
82511.e: In winds that are too strong, the blades could turn too fast. That is why they are stopped for protection.
82511.m: In storms, wind turbines are stopped for protection.

82512.q: Which toy turns like a little wind turbine when you blow on it?
82512.e: The pinwheel has light blades that even a breath can turn. It works like a big wind turbine.
82512.m: A pinwheel turns in the wind.

82513.q: On which Alpine pass have five large wind turbines been turning since 2020?
82513.e: In 2020 a wind farm with five turbines started operating near the Gotthard Hospice. It lies more than 2,000 metres above sea level.
82513.m: Wind power is made on the Gotthard too.

82514.q: What provides the power for a hydroelectric power station?
82514.e: The water rushes through the power station with great force. Its movement is turned into electricity.
82514.m: A hydroelectric power station makes electricity from moving water.

82515.q: What turns in a hydroelectric power station when the water rushes onto it?
82515.e: The water drives a turbine, similar to a paddle wheel. The turbine turns a generator that produces electricity.
82515.m: In the power station, water turns a turbine.

82516.q: Why is a large storage lake in the mountains useful for the electricity supply?
a: It holds water ready until electricity is needed
It holds the glaciers in place
82516.e: In summer, lots of meltwater is collected. In winter, when more electricity is needed, it is let through the power station.
82516.m: A storage lake saves water for later.

82517.q: How does the water get from the storage lake down to the power station in the valley?
a: Through thick pipes in the mountain
82517.e: The water shoots down the mountain through thick pipes or tunnels. At the bottom it drives the turbines with great force.
82517.m: Thick pipes carry the water to the power station.

82518.q: Where are run-of-river power stations located?
82518.e: Run-of-river power stations use the water that constantly flows in a river. Many are on the Rhine and the Aare, for example.
82518.m: Run-of-river power stations are on rivers.

82519.q: Where does the water in Alpine reservoirs mainly come from?
82519.e: In spring and summer, snow and glacier ice melt. The meltwater fills the reservoirs.
82519.m: Meltwater fills the reservoirs in the mountains.

82520.q: What was a mill by a stream, where the water turned a big wheel, called?
82520.e: The flowing water turned the mill wheel. That way grain could be ground or wood sawn without muscle power.
82520.m: Water mills used the power of water long ago.

82521.q: Why are fish ladders built at river power stations?
a: So fish can swim past the power station
So people can climb into the water
82521.e: Many fish migrate upstream. Using the fish ladder made of small pools, they get past the power station.
82521.m: Fish ladders help fish past obstacles.

82522.q: What should you do when you leave a room?
82522.e: Light in an empty room uses electricity without being useful. That is why you switch it off when you go out.
82522.m: Switch off the light when you leave the room.

82523.q: How do you save electricity with the TV?
a: Switch it off completely instead of standby
Leave it on all the time
82523.e: Even on standby, a device uses some electricity. Switching it off completely saves energy.
82523.m: Switching off saves more electricity than standby.

82524.q: Why should you not leave the fridge door open for long?
82524.e: When the door is open, warm air flows in. The fridge then has to cool for longer and uses more electricity.
82524.m: A closed fridge door saves electricity.

82525.q: What normally uses less hot water?
82525.e: A full bath needs much more hot water than a short shower. Heating water takes energy.

82526.q: What is the most energy-saving way to air a room in winter?
a: Briefly, with the window wide open
For hours with the window tilted
82526.e: When you air a room briefly with the window wide open, fresh air comes in fast, but the walls do not cool down. A tilted window loses a lot of heat.
82526.m: In winter, air rooms briefly and thoroughly.

82527.q: What is the coloured label that shows how economical a device is called?
82527.e: The energy label uses letters and colours to show how much energy a device uses. Green means economical.
82527.m: The energy label shows how economical a device is.

82528.q: How does washing dry without any electricity?
82528.e: On the line, sun and air dry the washing. A tumble dryer, on the other hand, uses a lot of electricity.
82528.m: The washing line needs no electricity.

82529.q: What do you do with the charger when the mobile phone is full?
82529.e: Some chargers use a little electricity even without a phone. That is why you unplug them after charging.

82530.q: What is the dynamo on a bike for?
a: It makes electricity for the lights
82530.e: The dynamo is driven by the turning wheel. It produces electricity for the bike lights.
82530.m: The dynamo makes electricity for the bike lights.

82531.q: Where does the bike dynamo get its energy from?
82531.e: Pedalling turns the wheel. The dynamo uses this movement to make electricity.
82531.m: With a dynamo, your legs make the electricity.

82532.q: What does a bike light with a standlight do when you stop at a junction?
a: It keeps shining for a while
82532.e: A small store in the lamp is charged while you ride. When you stop, it keeps the lamp shining for a few minutes.
82532.m: The standlight keeps shining when you stop.

82533.q: Where on a bike is a hub dynamo fitted?
a: In the middle of the front wheel
82533.e: The hub dynamo sits in the hub, in other words in the middle of the front wheel. It runs quietly and reliably, even in the rain.
82533.m: A hub dynamo sits in the middle of the wheel.

82534.q: Do you have to pedal a bit harder with the dynamo switched on?
a: No, you do not have to pedal at all
82534.e: The dynamo needs energy to make electricity. This energy comes from your legs, so pedalling is a bit harder.
82534.m: A dynamo needs a little leg power.

82535.q: What colour must the light at the front of a bike be?
82535.e: At the front, the bike light shines white so you can see the way and be seen. A different light shines towards the back.
82535.m: The front bike light is white.

82536.q: Why do people like to ride a bike with lights on even during the day?
82536.e: With lights, cyclists catch drivers’ attention sooner. That makes the road safer.
82536.m: Lights on your bike make you easier to see.

82537.q: What does a dynamo on a bike do?
a: It makes electricity for the light while you ride
It stores water for the ride
82537.e: The wheel turns a magnet inside the dynamo. This produces electricity that makes the lamp shine. The faster you ride, the brighter the light.
82537.m: A bike dynamo turns movement into electricity.

82538.q: What is inside a torch so that it shines?
82538.e: Batteries or a rechargeable battery supply the electricity for the lamp. That is why you can take it anywhere without a cable.
82538.m: A torch gets its electricity from batteries.

82539.q: What gives off the light in most modern torches?
82539.e: LED stands for light-emitting diode. It uses little electricity and lasts a very long time.

82540.q: Why does a torch shine more weakly after a long time?
82540.e: Batteries give off their energy bit by bit. When they are almost empty, the light gets weaker.
82540.m: A weak light shows the batteries are almost empty.

82541.q: How does a wind-up torch with a crank work?
a: You make the electricity by turning
You put it in the socket
82541.e: Inside the torch is a small generator. When you turn the crank, electricity is produced, with no battery at all.
82541.m: A wind-up torch makes its own electricity.

82542.q: What is a lamp you wear on your head with a strap called?
82542.e: A head torch always shines where you are looking. That way you have both hands free, for example when camping.
82542.m: With a head torch your hands are free.

82543.q: How many times a minute do you give a light signal in the alpine distress signal?
82543.e: In the alpine distress signal, you give six signals a minute, then pause for a minute. The reply is three signals a minute.
82543.m: The alpine distress signal is six signals a minute.

82544.q: Why does a torch belong in the emergency supplies at home?
82544.e: If the power goes off, the lights in the house stay dark. With a torch and batteries you can still see.
82544.m: A torch helps in a power cut.

82545.q: What does the shiny mirror behind the bulb of a torch do?
82545.e: The mirror is called a reflector. It throws the light forwards, creating a bright beam.
82545.m: The reflector focuses the light forwards.

82546.q: Why should you never shine a bright torch into someone’s eyes?
a: It dazzles and can harm the eyes
It empties the battery at once
82546.e: Very bright light dazzles, and afterwards you cannot see well for a while. Strong lamps can even harm the eyes.
82546.m: Never shine a light into someone’s eyes.

82547.q: What can a rechargeable battery do that a normal battery cannot?
82547.e: A rechargeable battery stores electricity and can be charged again many times. A normal battery runs flat and must then be disposed of.
82547.m: A rechargeable battery can be charged again and again.

82548.q: What do you use to charge a mobile phone’s battery?
82548.e: The charger takes electricity from the socket and passes it to the battery in a suitable form. There it is stored.
82548.m: You charge a mobile phone with a charger.

82549.q: What does the battery symbol at the top of the phone screen show?
82549.e: The fuller the symbol, the more charge is left in the battery. When it is almost empty, you should charge the phone.
82549.m: The battery symbol shows the charge level.

82550.q: Why should you not leave a phone or battery in a hot car in the sun?
82550.e: Great heat wears batteries out faster. In the worst case they can even become dangerous.
82550.m: Batteries do not like great heat.

82551.q: Which bike has a battery that helps when you pedal?
82551.e: On an e-bike, an electric motor powered by the battery helps drive the bike. That makes it easier to get up hills.
82551.m: An e-bike rides with the help of a battery.

82552.q: What do you do if a rechargeable battery is fat and swollen?
a: Stop using it and hand it in
82552.e: A swollen battery is damaged and can catch fire. You take it to a specialist shop or a collection point.
82552.m: Do not use swollen batteries any more.

82553.q: What happens to a mobile phone when the battery is completely empty?
82553.e: Without electricity from the battery, the phone cannot work. Only after charging can it be switched on again.
82553.m: When the battery is empty, the phone switches off.

82554.q: What do you call it when you simply lay a phone on a flat charging pad to charge it?
82554.e: With wireless charging, the energy flows from the charging pad into the phone without a plug. The phone has to lie exactly right on the pad.
82554.m: Some phones can charge without a cable.

a: A portable battery for charging on the go
82555.e: A power bank stores electricity. With it you can charge your phone on the go without a socket.
82555.m: With a power bank you can charge on the go.

82556.q: How many different digits are there in our number system?
82556.e: Our number system is a base-ten system. All numbers are written with ten different digits.
82556.m: We write all numbers with ten digits.

82557.e: 9 is the largest digit. 10 is already a number made of two digits.

82558.q: How many digits does the number 365 have?
82558.e: The number 365 is made of the digits 3, 6 and 5. That is three digits.

82559.q: Which digit is in the tens place in the number 47?
82559.e: In 47, the 4 stands for 4 tens and the 7 for 7 ones.
82559.m: In 47, the 4 is the tens digit.

82560.q: Which digit is in the ones place in the number 582?
82560.e: The ones place is on the far right. In 582, that is the 2.
82560.m: The ones place is on the far right.

82561.q: Where do our digits originally come from?
82561.e: Our digits were invented in India. They came to Europe through Arab scholars, which is why they are called Arabic numerals.
82561.m: Our digits originally come from India.

82562.q: How many different digits do you need to write the number 1111?
82562.e: The number 1111 is made of the digit 1 four times. So you only need one single digit.
82562.m: A number can contain the same digit several times.

82563.q: Which digit appears twice in the number 2026?
82563.e: The number 2026 is made of the digits 2, 0, 2 and 6. The 2 appears twice.

82564.q: Which number can you make with the digits 3 and 8 if it should be as large as possible?
82564.e: The larger digit goes at the front, in the tens place. That gives 83.
82564.m: The larger digit goes at the front.

82565.e: If you add zero, the number stays the same. 7 + 0 makes 7.
82565.m: Adding zero does not change a number.

82566.e: Any number times zero makes zero. Five times nothing is nothing.

82567.e: When you count backwards, 0 comes after 1.

82568.e: If you take exactly 9 away from 9, nothing is left. The answer is 0.
82568.m: A number minus itself makes zero.

82569.q: Which old number symbols had no zero?
82569.e: The Romans wrote numbers with letters such as I, V and X. They had no symbol for zero.
82569.m: The Romans had no symbol for zero.

82570.q: How many zeros does the number 100 have?
82570.e: The number 100 is written with a 1 and two zeros.

82571.q: What happens to the number 6 if you add a zero on the right?
82571.e: If you add a zero, the number becomes ten times as big. 6 becomes 60.
82571.m: Adding a zero makes a number ten times bigger.

82572.e: The smallest digit is 0. It stands for nothing.

82573.e: An abacus is a calculating tool with beads on rods. You slide the beads to count and calculate.
82573.m: You can do sums with an abacus.

82574.q: What do you slide back and forth on an abacus?
82574.e: On an abacus, beads are threaded onto rods or wires. You slide them back and forth.
82574.m: On an abacus you slide beads.

82575.q: How many beads per row does a school counting frame often have?
82575.e: A counting frame for children usually has ten rows of ten beads each. That fits our base-ten system.
82575.m: A school counting frame usually has ten beads per row.

82576.q: How many beads does a counting frame with 10 rows of 10 beads have?
82576.e: 10 rows of 10 beads make 10 times 10, so 100 beads.
82576.m: Ten times ten makes a hundred.

82577.q: Is the abacus a new or a very old invention?
a: It was invented ten years ago
82577.e: People were already calculating with the abacus well over a thousand years ago, for example in China and Japan.
82577.m: The abacus is a very old calculating tool.

82578.q: Does an abacus need electricity or batteries?
82578.e: The abacus works only with your hands. It is much older than any battery.

82579.q: Which device has mostly replaced the abacus in everyday life?
82579.e: Today most people calculate with a calculator or a mobile phone. In the past, people often used the abacus.
82579.m: The calculator has mostly replaced the abacus.

82580.q: On a counting frame, 3 beads are on the left and 4 more beads are pushed over. How many are there altogether?
82580.e: 3 beads and 4 beads make 3 + 4 together, so 7 beads.

82581.q: How many items are in a dozen?
82581.e: A dozen means twelve items. In the past, eggs were often counted in dozens.

82582.q: How many items are in half a dozen?
82582.e: A dozen is 12 items. Half of that is 6.
82582.m: Half a dozen is six items.

82583.q: How many eggs are two dozen eggs?
82583.e: A dozen is 12. Two dozen are 12 + 12, so 24.

82584.q: How many eggs are a dozen?
82584.e: A dozen is 12 items. That is why many egg boxes hold exactly 12 eggs.

82585.e: A dozen is 12 eggs. 12 + 12 + 12 makes 36, so it is 3 dozen.

82587.q: A box for a dozen eggs has 9 eggs in it. How many are missing?
82587.e: A dozen is 12 eggs. 12 − 9 makes 3, so 3 eggs are missing.
82587.m: With nine eggs, three are still missing from a dozen.

82588.q: A baker adds one extra bread roll free to a dozen rolls. How many rolls are there now?
82588.e: A dozen is 12 rolls. With one more roll it is 12 + 1 = 13. This is called a baker’s dozen.
82588.m: A baker’s dozen is thirteen items.

82589.q: How many socks are a pair of socks?
82589.e: A pair is always two things that belong together.

82590.q: How many hands do 4 children have altogether?
82590.e: Each child has a pair of hands, so 2. 4 times 2 makes 8 hands.

82591.q: Which things do you usually buy as a pair?
82591.e: You need gloves for both hands. That is why they come as a pair.
82591.m: You buy gloves as a pair.

82592.q: A beetle has three pairs of legs. How many legs is that?
82592.e: A pair is two legs. 3 times 2 makes 6 legs.

82594.q: Every child has a pair of ears. How many ears do 3 children have altogether?
82594.e: A pair is two ears. 3 times 2 makes 6 ears.
82594.m: We have a pair of ears.

82595.q: 7 children line up in twos. How many children are left on their own?
82595.e: 7 children make 3 pairs, which is 6 children. One child is left on their own.
82595.m: With an odd number, one is left over when you make pairs.

82596.q: In the card game pairs (Memory), what do you call two cards with the same picture?
82596.e: In pairs, you look for two matching cards. Two things that belong together are called a pair.
82596.m: In the game pairs, you look for matching pairs.

82597.q: Into how many halves is a domino divided?
82597.e: A domino has two halves. Each half has dots or no dot.

82598.q: How many tiles does a normal set of dominoes with at most 6 dots per half have?
82598.e: The usual set goes up to double six. Each combination appears once, which makes 28 tiles.
82598.m: A normal set of dominoes has 28 tiles.

82599.q: How many dots does the double-six domino have altogether?
82599.e: On the double six, each half has 6 dots. 6 + 6 makes 12 dots.
82599.m: The double-six domino has twelve dots.

82600.q: Which number does an empty half of a domino show?
82600.e: An empty half has no dots. It stands for the number zero.
82600.m: An empty domino half means zero.

82601.q: A domino has 2 and 5 dots. How many dots is that altogether?
82601.e: You add both halves together: 2 + 5 makes 7.

82602.q: In dominoes, which tile fits next to a half with 4 dots?
82602.e: In dominoes, you put halves with the same number of dots next to each other. Only a 4 fits next to a 4.
82602.m: In dominoes, you match the same numbers.

82603.q: In the domino effect, what happens when you push the first domino?
a: They all fall one after another
82603.e: When dominoes stand in a row, each falling domino pushes the next one. So they all fall over one after another.
82603.m: In the domino effect, one domino falls after another.

82604.q: How many dots does a domino with 3 and 3 dots have?
82604.e: Both halves have 3 dots. 3 + 3 makes 6 dots.

82607.e: “Thirty” means three tens, so 30. The number 13 is called “thirteen”.

82609.e: The number 1000 is called “a thousand”. It has three zeros.
82609.m: The number 1000 is called a thousand.

82610.q: How do you say the number 3 in French?
82610.e: In French you count un, deux, trois. So 3 is called “trois”.

82611.q: How do you say the number 5 in English?
82611.e: In English, the number 5 is called “five”.

82612.q: In a race, only one child finishes before Tim. Which place does Tim come?
82612.e: The first child to finish comes first. Tim comes straight after, so he is in second place. For places you need ordinal numbers.
82612.m: For places you need ordinal numbers.

82613.q: How many zeros does a million have?
82613.e: A million is written 1,000,000. That is six zeros.

82614.q: How do you write a million in digits?
82614.e: A million is a 1 with six zeros. It is written 1,000,000.

82615.q: In Switzerland, how are large numbers like 1'000'000 often separated when written?
82615.e: In Switzerland, people often put an apostrophe between each group of three digits. That makes large numbers easier to read.
82615.m: In Switzerland, thousands are often separated with an apostrophe.

82617.q: How much are two half millions together?
82617.e: Half a million is 500,000. Two of them make 1,000,000, which is one million.

82618.q: What is the number you get from a thousand million called?
82618.e: A thousand million make a billion. It has nine zeros.
82618.m: A thousand million is a billion.

82619.e: A millionaire owns at least a million francs or another currency. That is a lot of money.
82619.m: A millionaire owns at least a million.

82620.q: Which place in the rankings is the winner?
82620.e: In a ranking list, the best person is right at the top in 1st place.

82621.q: Which medal does second place get at the Olympic Games?
82621.e: Second place gets a silver medal. The winner gets gold.

82622.q: Which medal does third place get at the Olympic Games?
82622.e: Third place gets a bronze medal.

82623.q: How many people stand on a winners’ podium?
82623.e: The three best stand on the podium: 1st place in the middle, 2nd and 3rd place beside it.
82623.m: The three best stand on the podium.

82624.e: In a ski race, whoever takes the least time wins. The shortest time comes 1st.
82624.m: In a ski race, the shortest time wins.

82625.q: Anna has 8 points, Ben 5 points and Chiara 10 points. Who is in 1st place?
82625.e: Whoever has the most points is at the front. 10 points are more than 8 and 5.
82625.m: With points, whoever has the most wins.

82626.q: Lea has 7 points, Tim 4 points and Noah 9 points. Who is in last place?
82626.e: Tim has the fewest with 4 points. So he is in last place.
82626.m: Whoever has the fewest points is at the back.

82627.q: Which place comes straight after 4th place in a ranking?
82627.e: Places are counted in order. After 4th place comes 5th place.

82628.q: Is there a very biggest number of all?
82628.e: You can always add 1 to any number. So there is no biggest number.

82629.q: What does the symbol for infinity look like?
82629.e: The symbol for infinity is ∞. It looks like an 8 lying on its side.
82629.m: The symbol for infinity is an eight lying down.

82630.q: What do the three dots mean in “1, 2, 3, ...”?
82630.e: The three dots show that the sequence goes on. With numbers, it never comes to an end.
82630.m: Three dots after a number sequence mean that it goes on.

82631.e: You add 1 to 1000. That makes 1001. You can always keep counting like this.
82631.m: Every number has a next one.

82632.e: Infinite means that something never stops. It has no end.

82633.q: Are there infinitely many even numbers?
82633.e: After every even number, two steps later there is another even number. That never stops.
82633.m: There are infinitely many even numbers.

82634.q: Can you finish counting to infinity?
82634.e: If you count, you never reach an end, because there is always a next number. Even a computer cannot do it.
82634.m: Nobody can finish counting to infinity.

82635.q: What is bigger than any number you can write down?
82635.e: Every number, even a billion, has an end. Infinity is not an ordinary number; it means that things always go on.
82635.m: Infinity is bigger than any number.

82636.e: The postcode tells the post office which place a letter or parcel should go to.
82636.m: The postcode helps the post office deliver.

82637.e: Bern has the postcode 3000. Postcodes starting with 3 are in the Bern region.

82638.q: Which digit do the postcodes of the city of Zurich start with?
82638.e: The postcodes of the city of Zurich start with 80, for example 8001.

82639.q: Which digit do the postcodes of Geneva and Lausanne start with?
82639.e: In western Switzerland, postcodes start with 1, for example 1201 Geneva.
82639.m: In western Switzerland, postcodes start with 1.

82640.q: Where does the postcode go on a letter in Switzerland?
82640.e: In Switzerland you write the postcode before the town, for example “3000 Bern”.
82640.m: The postcode goes before the town name.

82642.q: Which neighbouring country also uses Swiss postcodes?
82642.e: Liechtenstein is part of the Swiss postcode system. Its postcodes start with 94.

82643.q: Which of these years has a 29 February?
82643.e: 2028 is a leap year. Only leap years have a 29 February.
82643.m: Only leap years have a 29 February.

82644.q: How many years are in a millennium?
82644.e: A millennium lasts a thousand years. We live in the third millennium.
82644.m: A millennium is a thousand years.

82645.q: Roughly how often is there a leap year?
82645.e: Almost always, every fourth year is a leap year. That keeps the calendar in step with the Earth.
82645.m: There is a leap year roughly every four years.

82646.q: Which year is written on the Swiss Federal Charter?
82646.e: The Federal Charter is dated the beginning of August 1291. That is why Switzerland celebrates its national day on 1 August.

82647.q: How many years are in a century?
82647.e: A century lasts 100 years. A decade is 10 years.
82647.m: A century is a hundred years.

82648.q: How many years are in a decade?

82649.e: Each new year is 1 more. 2026 + 1 makes 2027.

82650.q: A child was born in 2018. How old will they be in 2026?
82650.e: You work out 2026 − 2018. That makes 8 years.
82650.m: You work out age with a subtraction.

82651.q: Which digit do the postcodes in Ticino start with?
82651.e: In Ticino, postcodes start with 6, for example 6900 Lugano or 6500 Bellinzona.

82652.q: How many years are there between 2020 and 2026?
82652.e: You work out 2026 − 2020. That makes 6 years.
82652.m: You find the gap between years with subtraction.

82653.q: Who may read your diary if you do not allow it?
82653.e: A diary is part of your privacy. Nobody should read it without your permission.
82653.m: Nobody reads my diary without permission.

82654.q: How can you set who sees your posts in an app?
82654.e: In an app's settings you can often choose who may see something. Best of all, only friends and family.
82654.m: In the settings I decide who sees my things.

82655.q: What does “private” mean for a profile?
82655.e: A private profile can only be seen by people you have allowed. A public profile can be seen by everyone.
82655.m: Only my friends see a private profile.

82656.q: Is it OK to secretly look through another child's phone?
82656.e: Someone else's phone is part of their privacy. You always ask first.
82656.m: I only look at other people's phones with permission.

82657.q: What does “public” mean on the internet?
82657.e: Anyone on the internet can see public posts, strangers included.

82658.q: What should a child do if a game asks for their location?
82658.e: Your location shows where you are right now. Ask your parents first whether the game really needs it.
82658.m: When asked for my location, I ask my parents first.

82659.q: Who else can see a message that you send to lots of people?
82659.e: Anyone who gets a message can read it and forward it. That is why you think carefully first.
82659.m: All the recipients can read a message I send.

82660.q: Can the internet definitely forget something for ever when you delete it?
82660.e: Others may already have copied or saved something before you delete it. That is why the rule is: think first, then post.
82660.m: The internet does not forget so quickly.

82661.q: Which of these is a piece of personal data?
82661.e: Personal data tells something about you as a person. Your address shows where you live.
82661.m: My address is part of my personal data.

82662.q: Who do you give your phone number to on the internet?
82662.e: Your phone number is personal data. Strangers on the internet should not get it.
82662.m: I do not give my phone number to strangers.

82663.q: Which of these is more OK to show in a game?
82663.e: A made-up name says nothing about you. School, address and date of birth are personal data.
82663.m: A made-up name protects me in a game.

82664.q: Why should you not post the name of your school publicly?
82664.e: Anyone who knows the name of your school knows where you are during the day. That is none of a stranger's business.
82664.m: I do not post the name of my school publicly.

82665.q: What do you do if a website asks for your name and address?
82665.e: With personal data you ask your parents first. They know whether the site can be trusted.
82665.m: Before typing in my details, I ask my parents.

82666.q: Which photo gives away where you live?
a: In front of the house with the house number
82666.e: In a photo in front of your house, people might see the street and house number. That way someone could find out where you live.
82666.m: Photos can give away my address too.

82667.q: What is a secret you do not pass on when logging in?
82667.e: The password protects your account. Only you and your parents should know it.

82668.q: Who often collects data about you on the internet?
82668.e: Many apps and websites save what you click on and type in. That is why you give away only a little.
82668.m: Apps and websites often collect data.

82669.e: You use your username to log in to a game or an app. Others often see it.
82669.m: I log in with my username.

82670.e: “StarFox” says nothing about you. The others show a name, home town or address.
82670.m: A good username says nothing about me.

82671.q: What should a username not contain?
82671.e: Your full name is personal data. With it, strangers can find you more easily.
82671.m: My full name does not belong in my username.

82672.q: Why is your year of birth in a username not a good idea?
82672.e: A year like 2017 shows how old you are. Strangers do not need to know that.
82672.m: My age does not belong in my username.

82673.q: What is the difference between a username and a password?
82673.e: Others often see your username. The password, however, stays secret.
82673.m: The username is visible, the password stays secret.

82674.q: What do you call a small picture next to the username?
82674.e: The profile picture appears next to your name. Instead of a photo of yourself, it is better to use a picture or a character.
82674.m: For my profile picture I prefer a character.

82675.q: Who should help you think up a username?
82675.e: Parents help you find a safe name without personal data.
82675.m: My parents help me with my username.

82676.q: Which username gives away where you live?
82676.e: “Noah_Thun” shows the first name and the town of Thun. The other names give nothing away.
82676.m: A place name in my username gives away where I live.

82677.q: Do you know for sure who is behind a profile on the internet?
82677.e: On the internet people can use a fake photo and a fake name. That is why you never know for sure.
82677.m: On the internet anyone can pretend to be someone else.

82678.q: A stranger in a game wants to meet you. What do you do?
82678.e: Never meet people from the internet on your own. Tell your parents or another adult straight away.
82678.m: I talk to my parents about meeting strangers from the internet.

82679.q: A stranger writes: “This is our secret.” What do you do?
82679.e: Good friends do not ask you to keep secrets from your parents. Tell an adult you trust.
82679.m: I tell an adult about strange secrets.

82680.q: A stranger offers you presents in a game. What do you do?
a: Say no and tell your parents
82680.e: Strangers offering presents often want something back. Say no and talk to your parents.
82680.m: I refuse presents from strangers on the internet.

82681.q: Which function lets you block an unpleasant player?
82681.e: With “Block” the person can no longer write to you.

82682.q: What does the “Report” function do in an app?
a: It informs the people who run the app
82682.e: With “Report” you tell the people who run the app that someone is behaving badly. They can block that person.
82682.m: By reporting, I help make the app safer.

82683.q: Who may a child write to in a chat?
82683.e: It is safest to write only to people you also know in real life.
82683.m: I chat with people I really know.

82684.q: A stranger asks: “Are you home alone?” What is right?
82684.e: That is none of a stranger's business. Do not answer and tell your parents.
82684.m: I do not answer strangers' questions about my home.

82685.e: A chain letter tells you to forward the message to lots of other people.
82685.m: A chain letter wants me to pass it on.

82686.q: A chain letter threatens: “Send this on, or something will happen to you!” Is that true?
a: Yes, if you have read it
82686.e: Threats like that are made up. Nothing happens if you do not forward the chain letter.
82686.m: Threats in chain letters are made up.

82687.q: What is the best thing to do with a chain letter?
82687.e: You simply delete the chain letter. That way the chain stops with you.

82688.q: What do you do if a chain letter scares you?
82688.e: Talking to your parents or a teacher helps against the fear. They explain that the letter is not true.
82688.m: If a chain letter scares me, I talk to an adult.

82689.q: Why do chain letters reach so many people so quickly?
a: Everyone sends them to lots of people
82689.e: If everyone forwards to lots of people, the number of recipients grows very quickly.
82689.m: Chain letters spread because lots of people forward them.

82690.q: A chain letter promises good luck if you forward it. Is that true?
a: Yes, if you send it to ten people
Yes, if you send it quickly
82690.e: A chain letter cannot bring luck. The promise is only meant to make you forward it.
82690.m: Chain letters do not bring luck.

82691.q: Who has usually written a chain letter?
82691.e: You usually do not know who made up a chain letter. It has just been forwarded many times.
82691.m: You usually do not know who sent a chain letter first.

82692.q: What is a warning sign in a chain letter?
82692.e: Chain letters often threaten you or put you under time pressure. That is how you recognise them.
82692.m: Threats and time pressure are warning signs.

82693.q: Why do many free apps show adverts?
82693.e: Free apps often earn money with adverts. Companies pay for you to see the adverts.
82693.m: Free apps often earn money with adverts.

82694.q: A window flashes: “You have won! Click here!” What do you do?
82694.e: Prize messages like that are almost always tricks. You do not click them and you close the window.
82694.m: I do not click on fake prize messages.

82695.q: How can you often recognise adverts on the internet?
82695.e: Adverts are often marked with “Ad”, “Advertisement” or “Sponsored”.
82695.m: Adverts are often labelled with the word Ad.

82696.q: What is an influencer doing who praises a toy and gets money for it?
82696.e: If someone gets money or presents for praising a product, that is advertising.

82697.q: What is the safest way to close a pop-up advert?
82697.e: The small X at the top usually closes the window. Big colourful buttons often lead to more adverts.
82697.m: I close pop-up adverts with the small X.

82698.q: What is a short advertising film, for example before a video, called?
82698.e: An advert is a short film that praises a product. You see it on television or before videos on the internet.
82698.m: An advert is a short advertising film.

82699.q: Is everything adverts promise really true?
82699.e: Adverts show products looking especially good. In real life they are often smaller or less great.
82699.m: Adverts often show things looking better than they are.

82700.e: With an in-app purchase you pay inside a game or app, for example for coins or characters.
82700.m: An in-app purchase costs real money.

82701.q: Does a free app sometimes cost money after all?
82701.e: Many free apps sell extras inside the game. These cost real money.
82701.m: Free apps can cost money too.

82702.q: What do you do before you buy something in a game?
82702.e: You may only buy something with your parents' permission. It is real money.
82702.m: Before every purchase I ask my parents.

82703.q: Game coins cost 5 francs in the game. Is that real money?
82703.e: If you buy game coins with francs, you pay with real money. The money is gone afterwards.

82704.q: How can parents prevent in-app purchases?
82704.e: In the settings you can protect purchases with a password or a lock.
82704.m: A purchase lock protects against unwanted purchases.

82705.q: You buy 3 packs for 2 francs each. How much does that cost?
82705.e: 3 packs times 2 francs is 3 times 2, so 6 francs.
82705.m: Three times two francs makes six francs.

82706.q: A game says: “Only 1 minute left! Buy now!” What does it want?
82706.e: With time pressure the game wants you to buy quickly without thinking.
82706.m: Time pressure is meant to make me buy quickly.

82707.q: What is a surprise box in a game that you can buy called?
82707.e: A loot box is a surprise box. You do not know beforehand what is inside, but you pay anyway.
82707.m: With a loot box you do not know what you will get.

82708.q: What does an age rating on a game show?
a: From what age it is suitable
82708.e: The age rating says from what age a game or film is suitable.
82708.m: The age rating shows from what age something is suitable.

82709.q: Which age rating is suitable for a 7-year-old child?
82709.e: PEGI 7 means suitable from age 7. The other games are for older children or adults.
82709.m: PEGI 7 is suitable from age seven.

82710.q: What is the lowest PEGI age rating?
82710.e: PEGI 3 is the lowest rating. Games like that are fine even for small children.

82711.q: Which PEGI rating is only for adults?
82711.e: PEGI 18 means only from age 18. These games are for adults.

82712.q: Where do you find a game's age rating?
82712.e: The age rating is on the packaging and in the app store with the description.
82712.m: The age rating is on the packaging.

82713.e: Some games and films can frighten or overwhelm children. Age ratings protect them from that.

82714.q: A game is rated PEGI 12. May an 8-year-old child play it?
82714.e: PEGI 12 means only from age 12. A child of 8 is too young for it.
82714.m: For PEGI 12 you have to be at least twelve.

82715.q: How many years does a 9-year-old child still need to wait for PEGI 12?
82715.e: You calculate 12 minus 9. That makes 3 years.
82715.m: At nine, there are three years to go until PEGI 12.

82716.q: What do you do if you are treated meanly in the class chat?
82716.e: Get help from your parents or teachers. Insulting back usually makes it worse.
82716.m: If I am cyberbullied, I get help.

82717.q: Why should you not delete mean messages straight away?
82717.e: A screenshot of the messages serves as evidence. That way adults can help better.
82717.m: I save mean messages as evidence.

82718.q: Can cyberbullying happen in the evening and at the weekend too?
82718.e: Your phone is almost always with you. That is why cyberbullying can happen at any time, even at home.
82718.m: Cyberbullying can happen at any time.

82719.q: What do you do if you see someone else being picked on online?
82719.e: Bystanders can help too, by telling adults. Laughing along makes the bullying bigger.
82719.m: If others are being picked on, I get help.

82720.e: “Well done!” is kind. The other sentences hurt.
82720.m: On the internet I stay friendly.

82721.q: How does someone who is being bullied feel?
82721.e: Bullying hurts. People affected often feel sad, alone or afraid.

82722.q: Which rule applies on the internet just like in the playground?
82722.e: On the internet there are real people behind the screens. That is why respect matters there too.
82722.m: I am respectful on the internet too.

82723.q: Which telephone number helps children and young people in Switzerland with worries?
82723.e: The number 147 is the advice line for children and young people. The other numbers are emergency numbers.

82724.q: How much does a call to the number 147 cost?
82724.e: The advice line 147 is free. That way every child can call.

82725.q: Which foundation runs the advice line 147?
82725.e: The advice and help line 147 belongs to the foundation Pro Juventute.
82725.m: The number 147 belongs to Pro Juventute.

82726.q: Besides by phone, how can you reach the advice line 147?
82726.e: With 147 you can not only call, but also chat or write an email.

82727.e: The number 147 is there especially for children and young people.
82727.m: 147 is there for children and young people.

a: Only if there is a fire
82728.e: At 147 you can talk about anything that worries you, for example arguments, bullying or fear.
82728.m: At 147 I can talk about any worry.

82729.q: Which number do you dial if there is a fire?
82729.e: If there is a fire, you call the fire brigade on 118. 147 is there for worries and questions.

a: A message that is not true
82730.e: Fake news tells you something that is not true but looks real.
82730.m: Fake news looks real but is not true.

82731.q: What are false reports on the internet often called?
82731.e: False reports are called fake news. “Fake” means forged or not real.

82732.q: What do you do before you forward an amazing message?
82732.e: Before sharing, you ask adults or look it up in reliable sources.

82733.q: Where are you more likely to find correct news for children?
82733.e: Children's news on television or online is checked by experts.

82734.q: How can you often recognise fake news?
82734.e: Fake news often causes fear or anger, so that people forward it quickly.
82734.m: Fake news often wants to scare me.

82735.q: What is the source of a piece of news?
82735.e: The source shows who wrote a piece of news and where it comes from. Well-known sources are usually more reliable.
82735.m: With news, I look at the source.

82736.q: Who do you ask if you do not know whether a piece of news is true?
82736.e: Parents or teachers help you check whether a report is true.
82736.m: If I am in doubt, I ask an adult.

82737.q: What happens when lots of people share fake news?
82737.e: The more people share fake news, the more people believe it. But that does not make it true.
82737.m: Sharing fake news does not make it true.

82738.q: A friend sends you a photo of a child so you can laugh at them. What do you do?
a: Use it as your profile picture
82738.e: A photo meant for laughing at someone hurts that child. You do not forward it and you talk to an adult.
82738.m: I do not forward photos meant to laugh at someone.

82739.q: What is the right to decide about photos of yourself called?
a: The right to your own image
82739.e: The right to your own image means you decide whether a photo of you is shown.
82739.m: I have the right to my own image.

82740.q: Can you simply pass off a photo from the internet as your own?
82740.e: Whoever took a photo has rights to it. You do not pass it off as your own.
82740.m: I do not pass off other people's photos as my own.

82741.q: When is the best time to post holiday photos?
a: On the first day of the holiday
82741.e: Posting during your holiday shows everyone that nobody is at home. That is why it is better to wait until you are back.
82741.m: I only post holiday photos after the holiday.

82742.q: What do you do if someone shows an embarrassing photo of you?
82742.e: Adults can help get the photo deleted. You do not have to sort it out on your own.
82742.m: With embarrassing photos, I get help.

82743.q: May you secretly post a funny photo of your teacher?
82743.e: Teachers also have the right to their own image. You do not post it without permission.
82743.m: I only post photos of others with permission.

82744.q: Who is it best to send photos of yourself to?
82744.e: You only send photos to family and real friends. Strangers should not get photos of you.
82744.m: I only send photos of me to people I know.

82745.q: What can the background of a photo give away?
82745.e: In the background you often see street signs, buildings or the school. That way people know where you are.
82745.m: The background of a photo can give something away too.

82746.q: Which of these is not personal data?
82746.e: Everyone knows the capital, Bern; it says nothing about you. Birthday, mobile number and address are personal data.
82746.m: Personal data tells something about me.

82747.q: May you use a friend's username to pretend to be them?
82747.e: Pretending to be someone else is unfair and can harm them. Everyone uses only their own account.
82747.m: I only use my own account.

82748.q: A stranger wants you to switch to another app to chat privately. What do you do?
a: Say no and tell your parents
82748.e: Someone who wants to lure you into another app often wants nobody else to read along. Say no and tell your parents.
82748.m: I do not switch to other apps with strangers.

82749.q: What colour are the long petals of the oxeye daisy?
82749.e: The oxeye daisy has a ring of white petals. In the middle it is yellow.
82749.m: The oxeye daisy has white petals around a yellow middle.

82750.q: Which small flower does the oxeye daisy look very like, although it is much bigger?
82750.e: The oxeye daisy and the daisy are both white with a yellow middle. But the oxeye daisy is much bigger and has a long stem.
82750.m: The oxeye daisy looks like a big daisy.

82751.q: What is the yellow middle of an oxeye daisy made of?
82751.e: The yellow middle is made of lots and lots of tiny tube-shaped flowers. So an oxeye daisy is really a whole basket of flowers.
82751.m: An oxeye daisy is a little basket of many small flowers.

82752.q: What game do children often play with an oxeye daisy?
a: Pulling off the petals one by one
Using the flower as a whistle
Blowing the seeds into the air
Using the flower as a stamp
82752.e: In the well-known game you pull off one petal after another and say a sentence each time, taking turns between two. The last petal decides the result.
82752.m: You can play a petal-pulling game with oxeye daisies.

82753.q: In which meadows do especially many oxeye daisies grow?
82753.e: Oxeye daisies like poor meadows that get little fertiliser. There they have enough light and space.
82753.m: Oxeye daisies love poor meadows with little fertiliser.

82754.q: When do oxeye daisies mainly flower in our meadows?
82754.e: Oxeye daisies flower mainly in May and June, often later in the summer too.
82754.m: In early summer the meadows are white with oxeye daisies.

82755.q: About how tall does an oxeye daisy grow?
82755.e: The oxeye daisy usually grows about 30 to 60 centimetres tall. So it sticks out well above the grass.
82755.m: The oxeye daisy reaches about up to a child’s knee.

82756.q: Which animals like visiting the oxeye daisy?
82756.e: The open flower of the oxeye daisy is easy to reach. That is why lots of beetles, flies and bees land on it.
82756.m: Lots of different insects land on the oxeye daisy.

82757.q: What colour are the flowers of meadow clary usually?
82757.e: Meadow clary has bright blue-violet flowers. They grow in tiers one above the other on the stem.

82758.q: What shape is the stem of meadow clary?
82758.e: The stem of meadow clary has four edges. That is typical of the mint family.
82758.m: Meadow clary has a stem with four edges.

82759.q: What happens when a bumblebee crawls into a clary flower?
a: The flower falls off at once
82759.e: As it crawls in, the bumblebee presses against a lever. Then the stamens swing down and dab pollen onto its back.
82759.m: Meadow clary stamps pollen onto the bumblebee’s back.

82760.q: Which well-known garden herb is meadow clary related to?
82760.e: Meadow clary and common sage belong to the same genus. Both have a spicy smell.
82760.m: Meadow clary is a relative of common sage.

82761.q: Where does meadow clary like to grow best?
82761.e: Meadow clary loves sun and warmth. That is why you find it in dry meadows and on sunny banks.
82761.m: Meadow clary likes it sunny and dry.

82762.q: What does the shape of a single clary flower remind you of?
82762.e: The clary flower has an upper lip and a lower lip. That is why it belongs to the lipped flowers, the mint family.
82762.m: The clary flower looks like an open mouth with two lips.

82763.q: What does meadow clary smell like when you rub a leaf?
82763.e: The leaves of meadow clary contain scented substances. If you rub a leaf, it smells spicy.
82763.m: A rubbed clary leaf smells spicy.

82764.q: What leaves does meadow clary mainly have?
a: Big leaves down at the ground
82764.e: Meadow clary has most of its leaves down at the ground. They are wrinkly and form a rosette. Only a few small leaves grow on the stem.
82764.m: The big clary leaves lie down at the ground.

82765.q: Where are cornflowers often specially sown today?
a: In the woods under fir trees
82765.e: In many fields the cornflower has become rare. That is why today it is often sown in gardens and in flower strips at the edge of fields. Bees find food there too.
82765.m: Cornflowers are often sown in gardens and flower strips today.

82766.q: Why is the cornflower called that?
a: It often grows in fields of grain
Its seeds look like maize kernels
82766.e: In the past the cornflower grew in almost every field of grain. Grain is also called corn.
82766.m: The cornflower is called that because it grows in cornfields.

82767.q: Why has the cornflower become rare in many fields today?
82767.e: Farmers often spray weedkillers and clean their seed thoroughly. Because of this, the cornflower has become rare in many places.
82767.m: Weedkillers have made the cornflower rare.

82768.q: How long does a cornflower live?
82768.e: The cornflower is an annual. It sprouts, flowers, makes seeds and then dies.
82768.m: The cornflower lives only one year and survives through its seeds.

82769.q: What do the blue flowers of the cornflower attract?
82769.e: Large blue flowers sit around the edge of the cornflower. They attract bees, bumblebees and other insects.
82769.m: The blue flowers of the cornflower attract insects.

82770.q: Which plant family does the cornflower belong to?
82770.e: The cornflower belongs to the daisy family, like the oxeye daisy. Its flower is made of lots of small single flowers.
82770.m: The cornflower is a basket of many single flowers.

82771.q: What are dried cornflower petals often used for?
a: As a colourful ingredient in tea
82771.e: The dried blue flowers are often put in tea blends. They look pretty there.
82771.m: Blue cornflower petals make tea colourful.

82772.q: Next to which flower does the cornflower often grow at the edge of fields?
82772.e: Poppies and cornflowers often grow together by fields of grain. Both are typical field flowers.
82772.m: Poppies and cornflowers often flower together at the edge of fields.

82773.q: What colour is the common poppy?
82773.e: The common poppy has big, bright red petals. You can see it from far away.
82773.m: The common poppy is bright red.

82774.q: What colour is the spot at the base of the common poppy’s petals often?
82774.e: Many poppy flowers have a dark, almost black spot at the base of each petal.
82774.m: The red poppy often has black spots in the middle.

82775.q: What do the petals of the common poppy look like when they come out of the bud?
82775.e: In the bud the petals are tightly folded together. That is why they look crumpled at first.
82775.m: Fresh poppy petals are crumpled like thin paper.

82776.q: Where are the seeds of the common poppy?
82776.e: After flowering, the common poppy forms a capsule. It contains lots and lots of tiny seeds.
82776.m: Poppy seeds grow in a capsule.

82777.q: How do the seeds get out of the poppy capsule?
a: Like out of a salt shaker
The capsule melts in the rain
82777.e: There are small holes at the top of the capsule. When the wind shakes the plant, the seeds fall out like salt from a salt shaker.
82777.m: The poppy capsule scatters its seeds like a salt shaker.

82778.q: What do bees collect from the common poppy, since it has no nectar?
82778.e: The common poppy offers no nectar. But bees and bumblebees collect lots of pollen there.
82778.m: Bees collect pollen from the common poppy.

82779.q: About how long does a single poppy flower last?
82779.e: A single common poppy flower loses its petals after only a few days. But new buds keep opening.
82779.m: A poppy flower only lasts a short time.

82780.q: Why shouldn’t you eat the common poppy?
82780.e: The common poppy contains a milky sap with substances that are slightly poisonous. That is why people do not eat it.
82780.m: The common poppy is pretty, but not for eating.

82781.q: How many leaflets does a normal clover leaf have?
82781.e: A clover leaf is normally made of three small leaflets. That is why clover is called “Trifolium” in Latin, which means three leaves.
82781.m: A normal clover leaf has three parts.

82782.q: What does a clover leaf with four leaflets mean to many people?
82782.e: Four-leaf clovers are very rare. That is why they are thought to bring luck.
82782.m: A four-leaf clover is thought to bring luck.

82783.q: What colour are the flower heads of red clover?
82783.e: Red clover has round flower heads in pink to reddish purple. That is where its name comes from.
82783.m: Red clover has pink flower heads.

82784.q: Which animals especially like eating red clover in the pasture?
82784.e: Red clover is very good food for cows and other farm animals. That is why farmers often sow it specially.
82784.m: Cows especially like eating red clover.

82785.q: Which insect can easily reach the nectar of red clover with its long tongue?
82785.e: The nectar sits deep in the narrow tubes of the clover flowers. Bumblebees with long tongues can reach it easily.
82785.m: Bumblebees with long tongues drink nectar from red clover.

82786.q: What does red clover do for the soil?
82786.e: Tiny bacteria live on the roots of clover. They take nitrogen from the air and so fertilise the soil.
82786.m: Clover fertilises the soil with the help of tiny bacteria.

82787.q: What does it taste like if you suck on a single clover flower?
82787.e: There is a little nectar in the small clover flowers. That is why they taste slightly sweet.
82787.m: Clover flowers taste slightly sweet of nectar.

82788.q: What does the flower head of red clover look like?
a: Like a long ear of grain
82788.e: With red clover, lots of small flowers sit close together. Together they form a round head.
82788.m: Red clover flowers in round heads.

82789.q: Why is the bellflower called that?
a: Its flower looks like a bell
It flowers when the church bells ring
82789.e: The bellflower’s flower is shaped like a little bell. That is where its name comes from.

82790.q: What colour is the spreading bellflower usually?
82790.e: The spreading bellflower has pale blue-violet flowers. Rarely there are white flowers too.
82790.m: The spreading bellflower is usually blue-violet.

82791.q: Into how many points is the edge of a bellflower flower divided?
82791.e: The bell of the flower ends in five pointed tips. On the spreading bellflower they are wide open.
82791.m: The bellflower has five points around the edge of its flower.

82792.q: What does the bellflower’s Latin name “Campanula” mean?
82792.e: “Campana” is Latin for bell. So “Campanula” means little bell.
82792.m: Campanula is Latin and means little bell.

82793.q: Which animals sometimes spend the night in bellflowers?
82793.e: Some small wild bees, for example scissor bees, spend the night or rainy spells in the bells. They are protected there.
82793.m: Small wild bees sometimes sleep in bellflowers.

82794.q: In which months does the spreading bellflower mainly flower?
82794.e: The spreading bellflower flowers in early summer and summer, from about May to July.
82794.m: The spreading bellflower flowers in early summer.

82795.q: What is the stem of the spreading bellflower like?
82795.e: The spreading bellflower has a thin, delicate stem. That is why the flowers sway in even a light wind.
82795.m: The spreading bellflower stands on a thin stem.

82796.q: What colour are the flowers of the spreading bellflower mostly?
82796.e: The spreading bellflower has blue-violet bells. It grows in meadows and by paths.
82796.m: The spreading bellflower has blue-violet flowers.

82797.q: What colour are the flowers of the buttercup in the meadow?
82797.e: The meadow buttercup has bright yellow flowers. In spring it turns whole meadows yellow.
82797.m: The buttercup has bright yellow flowers.

82798.q: In German the buttercup is called “cock’s foot”. Why?
a: Its leaves look like a cockerel’s foot
It flowers when the cockerel crows
It only grows in the chicken yard
82798.e: The leaves of the buttercup are deeply cut. They remind you of a cockerel’s foot.
82798.m: Buttercup leaves look like a chicken’s foot.

82799.q: How do the petals of the buttercup shine?
82799.e: The yellow petals of the buttercup are very shiny, as if they had been varnished. The light is reflected by a special layer.
82799.m: The buttercup shines as if it were varnished.

82800.q: Why don’t cows eat fresh buttercups in the pasture?
82800.e: Fresh buttercups contain a sharp, poisonous substance. So cows leave them standing in the pasture.
82800.m: Fresh buttercups are poisonous, so cows leave them.

82801.q: How many petals does a meadow buttercup flower usually have?
82801.e: The yellow flower of the meadow buttercup usually has five petals.
82801.m: The buttercup usually has five yellow petals.

82803.q: What should you do after picking buttercups?
82803.e: The sap of the buttercup can irritate the skin. So you wash your hands after picking them.
82803.m: Wash your hands after picking buttercups.

82804.q: When are buttercups no longer dangerous for cows?
a: When they have been dried as hay
82804.e: When buttercups dry, the sharp substance is lost. So in hay they no longer harm cows.
82804.m: Dried buttercups in hay are harmless.

82805.q: What colour are the flowers of cow parsley?
82805.e: Cow parsley has lots of small white flowers. Because of this, some meadows look completely white in May.
82805.m: Cow parsley turns meadows white in May.

82806.q: How are the many small flowers of cow parsley arranged?
82806.e: With cow parsley, the small flowers sit on stalks that all start from one point. This forms an umbrella, which is called an umbel.
82806.m: Cow parsley flowers in white umbrellas.

82807.q: What is the stem of cow parsley like inside?
a: Full of juice like an orange
82807.e: The stem of cow parsley is hollow inside like a little tube. On the outside it has grooves.
82807.m: Cow parsley has a hollow stem.

82808.q: Why shouldn’t children pick and eat plants like cow parsley?
82808.e: Cow parsley looks like some very poisonous umbellifers such as hemlock. That is why you never eat white umbrella flowers from the meadow.
82808.m: Don’t eat white umbrella flowers from the meadow.

82809.q: What do the leaves of cow parsley look like?
a: Long like a blade of grass
82809.e: The leaves of cow parsley are finely divided. They remind you of the fronds of a fern.
82809.m: Cow parsley has fine leaves like a fern.

82810.q: In which meadows does cow parsley grow especially often?
82810.e: Cow parsley loves meadows with lots of fertiliser. There it grows fast and becomes very common.
82810.m: Where lots of fertiliser is used, lots of cow parsley grows.

82811.q: How tall can cow parsley grow?
82811.e: Cow parsley often grows hip-high and can reach up to about 1.5 metres.
82811.m: Cow parsley can grow as tall as a child.

82812.q: When does cow parsley flower, as one of the first big meadow flowers?
82812.e: Cow parsley flowers early in the year, from April and above all in May. So it comes before many other meadow flowers.
82812.m: Cow parsley already flowers in spring.

82813.q: What does the daisy do in the evening?
82813.e: In the evening and when it rains, the daisy folds up its white petals. In the morning it opens again.
82813.m: The daisy closes in the evening.

82814.q: When can you see daisies in flower?
82814.e: Daisies flower for a very long time. On mild days you can even see them in winter.
82814.m: Daisies flower almost all year round.

82815.q: Why does the daisy survive lawn mowing well?
a: Its leaves lie flat on the ground
It only grows in the shade
82815.e: The daisy’s leaves form a flat rosette on the ground. The lawnmower passes over it.
82815.m: With its flat leaves the daisy survives the lawnmower.

82816.q: What can you make from lots of daisies?
82816.e: Children join the stalks of daisies together. This makes a pretty crown or a daisy chain.
82816.m: You can make daisy chains from daisies.

a: Only animals in the zoo can
82817.e: Daisies are edible. You can sprinkle them on a salad, for example, but only from clean meadows.

82818.q: Which way do daisies turn during the day?
82818.e: Daisies turn their flowers towards the sun. That way they get lots of light and warmth.

82819.q: About how tall does a daisy grow?
82819.e: The daisy stays small and usually grows only about 5 to 15 centimetres tall.
82819.m: The daisy is a small flower.

82820.q: How long does a daisy live?
82820.e: The daisy is a perennial. It grows in the same place for several years.
82820.m: A daisy lives for several years.

82821.q: What colour are the flowers of yarrow usually?
82821.e: Yarrow usually has white flowers. Sometimes the flowers are pale pink too.

82822.q: What do the leaves of yarrow look like?
82822.e: The leaves of yarrow are very finely divided. They look like little green feathers.
82822.m: Yarrow has leaves like fine feathers.

82823.q: How are the many small flowers of yarrow arranged?
a: As a flat disc at the top
One by one on the ground
82823.e: Yarrow has lots of small flower heads. Together they form a flat, umbrella-like disc at the top.
82823.m: Yarrow has a flat disc of flowers at the top.

82824.q: Which animal is hidden in yarrow’s German name, “Schafgarbe”?
82824.e: The German name of yarrow contains the word for sheep. People say that sheep like eating the plant.
82824.m: Yarrow’s German name contains the sheep.

82825.q: What has yarrow been used for for a long time?
a: As a medicinal plant for tea
82825.e: People have been making tea from yarrow for a very long time. It is said to help with tummy ache, for example.
82825.m: Yarrow is an old medicinal plant.

82826.q: What does yarrow smell like when you rub it?
82826.e: Yarrow contains scented oils. When you rub it, it smells strongly spicy and a little bitter.

82827.q: Which hero from an old Greek legend is yarrow named after in Latin?
82827.e: The Latin name is “Achillea”. According to the legend, Achilles treated wounds with the plant.
82827.m: Yarrow bears the name of the hero Achilles.

82828.q: How well does yarrow cope with dry weather?
82828.e: Yarrow is very tough. It even grows at the dry edges of paths and meadows.
82828.m: Yarrow is tough and likes it dry.

82829.q: What colour is the flower of goat’s-beard?
82829.e: Goat’s-beard has a yellow flower. It looks a little like a dandelion.

82830.q: When does goat’s-beard close its flower?
82830.e: The flower of goat’s-beard is only open for a few hours a day. Around midday it closes again.

82831.q: What does the seed head of goat’s-beard look like?
82831.e: After flowering, goat’s-beard forms a big, round seed head like a dandelion clock. It is much bigger than the dandelion’s.
82831.m: Goat’s-beard forms a giant dandelion clock.

82832.q: How do the seeds of goat’s-beard travel?
82832.e: Each seed has an umbrella of fine hairs. With it, it flies away on the wind.
82832.m: Goat’s-beard seeds fly on the wind.

82833.q: What do the leaves of goat’s-beard look like?
82833.e: The leaves of goat’s-beard are long and narrow. Without its flower, the plant is easily mistaken for grass.
82833.m: Goat’s-beard has leaves like blades of grass.

82834.q: Which animal is in the name goat’s-beard?
82834.e: After flowering, fine hairs stick out of the covering. This reminds people of a billy goat’s beard. That is where the name comes from.
82834.m: Goat’s-beard reminds people of a billy goat’s beard.

82835.q: What comes out if you break the stem of goat’s-beard?
82835.e: White milky sap flows in the stem of goat’s-beard, just as in the dandelion.
82835.m: Goat’s-beard has white milky sap in its stem.

82836.q: About how tall does goat’s-beard grow?
82836.e: Goat’s-beard usually grows about 30 to 70 centimetres tall. So it stands out clearly among the grasses.
82836.m: Goat’s-beard grows about as tall as the grasses.

82837.e: Ragged-robin has pink to rose-red flowers. Rarely there are white flowers too.

82838.q: What do the petals of ragged-robin look like?
82838.e: Each petal of ragged-robin is divided into four narrow tips. That is why the flower looks tattered.

82839.q: In German, ragged-robin is called “cuckoo campion”. Which bird is in its German name?
82839.e: The plant flowers at about the time when you hear the cuckoo calling in spring. That is where part of its German name comes from.
82839.m: Ragged-robin flowers when the cuckoo calls.

82840.q: In which meadows does ragged-robin like to grow best?
82840.e: Ragged-robin loves wet soil. You find it mainly in damp meadows and by ditches.

82841.q: What do you often find on the stem of ragged-robin?
82841.e: Blobs of foam often sit on the stem. The larva of the froghopper hides inside. The foam is also called “cuckoo spit”.
82841.m: The foam on the stem protects the larva of an insect.

82842.e: The nectar sits deep in a narrow tube. Butterflies and bumblebees reach it with their long tongues.
82842.m: Insects with long tongues get nectar from ragged-robin.

82843.q: Why has ragged-robin disappeared from many places?
a: Many wet meadows have been drained
82843.e: Many wet meadows have been drained so that they can be used better. Because of this, ragged-robin loses its places to grow.

82844.q: In which month does ragged-robin usually start to flower?
82844.e: Ragged-robin flowers mainly in May and June, in early summer.

82846.q: How many petals does a common poppy flower have?
82846.e: The common poppy flower has four big red petals. Two are a little bigger than the other two.
82846.m: The common poppy has four red petals.

82847.q: When can you see yellow buttercups flowering in the meadows?
82847.e: The buttercup flowers from spring to summer. Then many meadows are speckled with yellow.
82847.m: The buttercup flowers in spring and summer.

82848.q: Which plant family does red clover belong to, like peas and beans?
82848.e: Like peas and beans, red clover belongs to the legumes. Its seeds grow in small pods.
82848.m: Red clover is a relative of peas and beans.

82849.q: After which country did Marie Curie name a newly discovered element?
82849.e: Marie Curie called the element polonium. The name is a reminder of her home country, Poland.
82849.m: The element polonium is named after Poland.

82850.q: How many Nobel Prizes did Marie Curie win?
82850.e: Marie Curie received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903 and the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1911.
82850.m: Marie Curie won two Nobel Prizes.

82851.q: What was Marie Curie the very first woman to become?
82851.e: In 1903 Marie Curie was the first woman to receive a Nobel Prize.
82851.m: Marie Curie was the first woman with a Nobel Prize.

82852.q: What did Marie Curie’s daughter later receive too?
82852.e: Her daughter Irène Joliot-Curie received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry together with her husband in 1935.
82852.m: Marie Curie’s daughter also won a Nobel Prize.

82853.q: Why did Marie Curie become ill because of her research?
82853.e: For many years Marie Curie worked with radioactive substances without protection. At that time the danger was hardly known.
82853.m: Radioactive radiation can make you ill.

82854.q: Thanks to Marie Curie, what did doctors use in the First World War to examine wounded soldiers?
82854.e: Marie Curie made sure that cars with X-ray machines drove to the wounded. That way doctors could see broken bones and splinters.
82854.m: Marie Curie brought X-ray machines to the wounded.

82855.q: In which Swiss city did Albert Einstein work at the patent office?
82855.e: From 1902 Einstein worked at the patent office in Bern. There he also wrote his famous papers of 1905.
82855.m: Einstein worked at the patent office in Bern.

82856.q: At which university in Zurich did Albert Einstein study?
82856.e: Einstein studied at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Zurich, ETH for short. At that time it was still called the Polytechnikum. He qualified there as a teacher of physics and mathematics.
82856.m: Einstein studied at ETH in Zurich.

82857.q: Which famous theory comes from Albert Einstein?
82857.e: Einstein developed the theory of relativity. It explains how space, time and gravity are connected.
82857.m: Einstein developed the theory of relativity.

82858.q: Which musical instrument did Albert Einstein like to play?
82858.e: All his life Einstein loved playing the violin. Music helped him think.
82858.m: Einstein liked to play the violin.

82859.q: Which country made Albert Einstein its citizen in 1901?
82859.e: Einstein became a Swiss citizen in 1901. He kept his Swiss citizenship all his life.

82860.q: What can you visit on Kramgasse in Bern?
82860.e: Einstein lived with his family in a flat on Kramgasse in Bern. Today the Einstein House, a small museum, is there.
82860.m: In Bern you can visit Einstein’s flat.

82861.q: In which Swiss town did Albert Einstein pass his school-leaving exam (Matura)?
82861.e: Einstein attended the cantonal school in Aarau and finished it in 1896 with the Matura.
82861.m: Einstein went to the cantonal school in Aarau.

82862.q: What is a well-known photo of Albert Einstein famous for?
a: He is sticking his tongue out
He is standing on the Moon
82862.e: In a famous photo from 1951 Einstein cheekily sticks out his tongue. The picture is on many posters today.
82862.m: A famous photo shows Einstein sticking out his tongue.

82863.q: On which ship did Charles Darwin travel around the world?
82863.e: As a young man Darwin travelled around the world on the survey ship HMS Beagle.
82863.m: Darwin travelled around the world on the Beagle.

82864.q: On which islands did Darwin observe special finches and giant tortoises?
82864.e: On the Galápagos Islands Darwin collected finches. Later it was realised that their beaks were different depending on the island.
82864.m: On the Galápagos Islands Darwin gathered important ideas.

82865.q: With the finches, how did Darwin tell what the birds fed on?
a: From the shape of their beaks
From the colour of their eggs
From the length of their legs
82865.e: Finches with thick beaks crack seeds, finches with thin beaks catch insects. The beak suits the food.
82865.m: A bird’s beak suits its food.

82866.q: What does Darwin’s famous idea explain?
82866.e: Darwin explained that living things change over a very long time. This development is called evolution.
82866.m: Living things change over a very long time.

82867.q: Roughly how long did Darwin’s voyage on the Beagle last?
82867.e: The Beagle set off at the end of 1831 and came back in 1836. The voyage lasted almost five years.
