84288.e: Very dense ice contains hardly any air bubbles. It absorbs red light and therefore looks blue.

a: Ice pushed together on the sea
84289.e: When wind and currents push sheets of ice together on the sea, pack ice forms. It can pile up high.
84289.m: Pack ice is sea ice pushed together.

84290.q: What are ships called that can force their way through thick ice?
84290.e: Icebreakers have a very strong hull. They drive up onto the ice and break it with their weight.
84290.m: An icebreaker breaks a path through the ice.

84291.q: What does the polar bear mainly hunt on the pack ice?
84291.e: Polar bears lie in wait for seals at breathing holes in the ice. Without sea ice they find much less food.
84291.m: Polar bears hunt seals on the ice.

84292.q: What happens to the sea ice in the Arctic every summer?
84292.e: It is warmer in summer, so part of the sea ice melts. In winter it freezes over again.
84292.m: In summer, part of the sea ice melts.

84293.q: What is a single flat sheet of ice drifting on the water called?
84293.e: Ice floes are flat pieces of sea ice. Seals like to rest on them.
84293.m: An ice floe is a flat sheet of ice on the water.

84294.q: Why did the explorer Fridtjof Nansen let his ship freeze into the pack ice on purpose from 1893?
a: To drift with the ice across the Arctic Ocean
To repair the ship in peace
84294.e: Nansen let his ship Fram freeze into the ice and drift with it. That is how he explored the Arctic Ocean.
84294.m: Nansen drifted through the Arctic ice in the Fram.

84295.q: Is there more or less sea ice in the Arctic today than 50 years ago?
84295.e: Satellite images show that the sea ice in summer has become much smaller. This is linked to global warming.
84295.m: The Arctic sea ice keeps shrinking.

84296.q: What happened in Antarctica in 1915 to the ship Endurance of the polar explorer Ernest Shackleton?
a: It was crushed by the pack ice
It was the first ship to reach the South Pole
84296.e: The Endurance got stuck in the ice in Antarctica and was crushed. Even so, all the men of the crew survived.
84296.m: Shackleton's Endurance was crushed by the ice.

84297.q: What happens to the sea level when a lot of ice on land melts?
84297.e: Meltwater from glaciers flows into the sea. This means there is more water and the sea level rises.
84297.m: When ice on land melts, the sea level rises.

84298.q: Which islands are especially threatened by rising sea levels?
84298.e: Most of the islands of the Maldives are only about one metre above the sea. If the water rises, they could be flooded.
84298.m: Low islands are threatened by the rising sea.

84299.q: How do the Netherlands protect their land from the sea?
84299.e: Dykes are long banks of earth and stone. They keep the sea away from the low-lying land.
84299.m: Dykes protect the land from the sea.

84300.q: What does “metres above sea level” mean for a mountain?
a: How high it is above the level of the sea
How far it is from the sea
How deep the sea next to it is
How long it takes to drive to the sea
84300.e: Heights are measured from the surface of the sea. That way all the mountains in the world can be compared.
84300.m: Heights are measured from sea level.

84301.q: Which city in Italy is often under water when the sea is high?
84301.e: Venice is built on many islands in a lagoon. During high water, called “acqua alta”, squares are flooded.
84301.m: Venice is often flooded at high water.

84302.q: What height is sea level on maps?
84302.e: Sea level is the zero point for all heights. Anything higher has a positive height.

84303.q: What can happen more often on coasts when the sea level is higher?
84303.e: If the sea is higher, it gets into the land more easily during storms. Then floods happen more often.
84303.m: A higher sea brings more floods to the coasts.

84304.q: What are the walls of a greenhouse usually made of?
84304.e: The walls have to let the sunlight in. That is why they are made of glass or clear plastic.

84305.q: Why is it warmer in a greenhouse than outside?
a: Sunlight gets in and the heat stays inside
The plants breathe out warm air
There is a fire hidden in the ground
84305.e: The sunlight warms the soil and the plants. The warm air can hardly escape through the glass.
84305.m: In a greenhouse, the sun's warmth is trapped.

84306.q: Which vegetable is often grown in greenhouses in Switzerland?
84306.e: Tomatoes like it warm. In greenhouses they grow even when it is cool outside.
84306.m: Tomatoes grow well in a greenhouse.

84307.q: What is another word for a greenhouse?
84307.e: Greenhouse and glasshouse mean the same thing. Plants are grown in the warmth inside.
84307.m: A greenhouse is also called a glasshouse.

84308.q: What happens in a car that stands in the sun in summer with the windows closed?
a: It stays as warm as outside
84308.e: Just like in a greenhouse, the sun shines through the windows and the heat stays inside. That is why you must never leave children or animals in the car.
84308.m: A car in the sun gets as hot as a greenhouse inside.

84309.q: Why does a gardener open the greenhouse windows on hot days?
a: So it does not get too hot for the plants
84309.e: In strong sunshine it can get too hot in the greenhouse. Fresh air cools the plants down.
84309.m: Letting air in protects greenhouse plants from heat.

84310.q: When is a greenhouse especially useful?
a: In spring, when it is still cold outside
In high summer in great heat
84310.e: In a greenhouse you can sow seeds early in the year. The young plants are protected from frost.
84310.m: A greenhouse protects young plants from the cold.

84311.q: What in the Earth's atmosphere works in a similar way to the glass of a greenhouse?
84311.e: Some gases in the air hold back heat, a bit like glass. This is called the greenhouse effect.
84311.m: Gases in the air keep the Earth warm like a greenhouse.

84312.q: Which metal is steel mainly made from?
84312.e: Steel is iron with a little carbon. This makes it stronger and tougher.
84312.m: Steel is mainly made of iron.

84313.q: Which metal does our blood need to carry oxygen?
84313.e: The red pigment in blood contains iron. It binds oxygen and carries it all round the body.
84313.m: The red pigment in blood contains iron.

84314.q: Where does the iron that nails are made from come from?
84314.e: Iron is found in certain rocks called iron ore. They are dug out of the ground and the iron is melted out.
84314.m: Iron comes from rocks in the ground.

84315.q: Where is iron ore melted into iron?
84315.e: A blast furnace is a huge furnace that gets very hot. Inside it, the ore turns into liquid iron.
84315.m: In a blast furnace, iron ore becomes iron.

84316.q: What happens to iron if it lies outside in the rain for a long time?
84316.e: Water and air attack the iron. Brown rust forms.

84317.q: Which famous tower in Paris is built of iron?
84317.e: The Eiffel Tower was built in 1889 from many thousands of iron parts. They are held together with rivets.
84317.m: The Eiffel Tower in Paris is made of iron.

84318.q: What happens to an iron nail that you put in water?
84318.e: Iron is much heavier than the same amount of water. That is why an iron nail sinks at once.
84318.m: An iron nail sinks in water.

84319.q: What happens if you stroke an iron nail many times in the same direction with a magnet?
84319.e: Stroking turns the nail itself into a weak magnet. Then it can pick up small paper clips.
84319.m: An iron nail can become a magnet itself.

84320.q: What are heavy, dark frying pans often made of?
84320.e: Cast iron is iron that is poured into a mould while liquid. Such pans are heavy and hold the heat for a long time.
84320.m: Heavy frying pans are often made of cast iron.

84321.q: What colour is freshly polished copper?
84321.e: Copper is one of the few metals with a colour of its own. It shines reddish brown.

84323.q: Which reddish metal are some expensive cooking pots made of?
84323.e: Copper pots shine reddish. Cooks like them because they heat up quickly and evenly.
84323.m: Some cooking pots are made of copper.

84324.q: Why are some pan bases made of copper?
84324.e: Copper passes on the heat from the hob quickly. This makes the whole pan evenly hot.

84325.q: Which metal is the outer skin of the Statue of Liberty in New York made of?
84325.e: The Statue of Liberty has a skin of thin copper sheets. It used to shine reddish brown, but today it is green.
84325.m: The Statue of Liberty is made of copper on the outside.

84326.q: What is the period called when people first made tools from copper?
84326.e: Copper was one of the first metals people used. The Copper Age lies at the end of the New Stone Age.
84326.m: In the Copper Age, people made their first tools from copper.

84327.q: What can you easily do with a thin copper wire?
84327.e: Copper is soft and bends well. That is why you can shape figures from copper wire.

84328.q: What is copper wire very often used for in the home?
84328.e: Electric cables contain copper wires. Copper conducts electricity very well.

84329.q: What does pure, polished silver look like?
84329.e: Silver is a bright, white, shiny metal. It reflects light very well.

84330.q: What happens to silver cutlery that lies in the drawer for a long time?
84330.e: Silver reacts with traces of sulphur in the air. This forms a dark layer; we say it tarnishes.
84330.m: Silver tarnishes and goes dark over time.

84331.q: How does tarnished silver become shiny again?
84331.e: When polishing, you rub away the dark layer. Afterwards the silver shines brightly again.
84331.m: Polishing makes tarnished silver beautiful again.

84332.q: Which place gets a silver medal at the Olympic Games?
84332.e: The silver medal is for second place. The winner gets the gold medal.

84333.q: Which metal is more expensive than silver?
84333.e: Gold is much rarer than silver. That is why it costs a great deal more per gram.
84333.m: Gold is more valuable than silver.

84334.q: Which metal conducts electricity best of all?
84334.e: Silver conducts electricity even better than copper. But because it is expensive, copper is usually used for cables.
84334.m: Silver conducts electricity best of all metals.

84335.q: What is the wedding anniversary after 25 years of marriage called?
84335.e: After 25 years of marriage, people celebrate their silver wedding. After 50 years it is the golden wedding.
84335.m: After 25 years, people celebrate their silver wedding.

84336.q: What is silver especially often used for?
84336.e: Silver shines beautifully and does not rust. That is why rings, necklaces and earrings are often made from it.
84336.m: Jewellery is often made from silver.

84337.q: Which of these metals is especially light?
84337.e: Aluminium weighs only about a third as much as the same amount of iron. That is why it is called a light metal.

84338.q: What are many drinks cans made of?
84338.e: Drinks cans are usually made of thin aluminium. They are light and protect the drink well.
84338.m: Many drinks cans are made of aluminium.

84339.q: Which rock is aluminium obtained from?
84339.e: Bauxite is a reddish rock with a lot of aluminium in it. Using a lot of electricity, aluminium is made from it.

84340.q: What are large parts of many aeroplanes made of?
84340.e: An aeroplane has to be strong but still light. That is why many parts are made of aluminium.
84340.m: Many aeroplane parts are made of aluminium.

84341.q: What do you save when you recycle old aluminium?
84341.e: Making new aluminium takes a great deal of electricity. Melting down old aluminium needs only a small part of that.
84341.m: Recycling aluminium saves a lot of energy.

84342.e: In air, aluminium forms a very thin protective layer. This protects the metal, so it does not rust.

84343.q: What are light bike frames often made of?
84343.e: Aluminium bike frames are strong and light. That way you can easily carry the bike.
84343.m: Light bike frames are often made of aluminium.

84344.e: Aluminium is a shiny, silvery grey metal. It looks a bit like silver but is much cheaper.

84345.q: Which small toy figures used to be cast from a soft, silvery metal?
84345.e: Tin figures are made by pouring liquid tin into moulds. Tin soldiers used to be a popular toy.
84345.m: Tin figures are cast from tin.

84346.q: Which of these metals melts at quite a low heat?
84346.e: Tin melts at only about 232 degrees. Iron and copper need well over 1000 degrees.
84346.m: Tin melts at a low heat.

84347.e: Tin is a shiny, silvery white metal. It looks a bit like silver.

84348.q: What do you use to join electric wires when soldering?
84348.e: Solder melts on the hot soldering iron and flows around the wires. As it cools, it sets and holds them together.
84348.m: When soldering, wires are joined with solder.

84349.q: What were many plates, mugs and jugs made of in the past?
84349.e: Tinware used to be found in many households. Today it is often collected as an ornament.
84349.m: In the past, people often ate from tin plates.

84350.q: Which soft metal makes a faint crackling sound when you bend a bar of it?
84350.e: When bending, the tiny crystals in the tin rub against each other. This makes a faint crackle called the ‘tin cry’.
84350.m: Tin crackles when you bend it.

84351.q: What can happen to objects made of pure tin if they are exposed to great cold for a very long time?
84351.e: In great cold, tin can slowly crumble into a grey powder. This is called tin pest.
84351.m: Tin can crumble in great cold.

84352.e: Pure tin is a soft metal. It is easy to bend and shape.

84353.q: Which place gets the bronze medal in a competition?
84353.e: In many competitions the three best get a medal. The bronze medal is for third place.

84354.q: Which period came before the Bronze Age?
84354.e: At first people made tools from stone. Only later did they learn to make bronze.
84354.m: The Stone Age came before the Bronze Age.

84355.e: New bronze shines golden brown. Over time it often becomes darker or greenish.

84356.q: What are many church bells cast from?
84356.e: Bronze bells sound especially beautiful and ring for a long time. This mixture is also called bell bronze.
84356.m: Many church bells are made of bronze.

84357.q: What are many large outdoor monuments and statues made of?
84357.e: Bronze withstands wind and weather for many hundreds of years. That is why monuments are often cast from it.
84357.m: Many monuments are cast in bronze.

84358.e: Bronze is made by mixing liquid metals together. Such a mixture is called an alloy.
84358.m: Bronze is a mixture of metals.

84359.q: Why was bronze better than pure copper for tools?
84359.e: Pure copper is quite soft. Bronze is much harder, so knives and axes stayed sharp for longer.

84360.q: What do you call pouring liquid bronze into a mould?
84360.e: The bronze is melted and poured into a mould. When it has cooled, it has taken on the shape.

84361.q: What were the villages on Swiss lake shores called where people lived in the Bronze Age?
84361.e: The houses stood on wooden stilts on the lake shore. Remains of them can still be found in many Swiss lakes today.
84361.m: In the Bronze Age, people in Switzerland lived in stilt houses.

84362.e: Rust is a reddish brown layer on iron. You can easily recognise it by its colour.

84363.q: Where does a bike rust faster?
84363.e: Iron rusts when water and air get to it. In the rain this happens much faster than in the dry.

84364.q: Which of these metals can rust?
84364.e: Rust only forms on iron and steel. Other metals change in other ways or hardly at all.

84365.q: How do you protect an iron garden gate from rust?
a: You stand it in the sun
84365.e: The paint keeps water and air away from the iron. That way the iron cannot rust so quickly.

84366.q: What happens to iron that rusts for years?
a: It becomes brittle and falls apart
84366.e: Rust eats deeper and deeper into the iron. In the end the iron gets holes and crumbles.

84367.q: Why do cars rust faster in winter?
a: Because of the snow on the roof
84367.e: In winter, salt is spread on Swiss roads. Salty water makes iron rust much faster.
84367.m: Road salt makes cars rust faster.

84368.q: What is the kitchen sink often made of, because it does not rust?
84368.e: Stainless steel is a steel that does not rust. It stays shiny even with lots of water.

84369.q: What helps to stop a bike chain from rusting?
84369.e: The oil forms a film on the chain. That way no water can reach the metal.
84369.m: Oil protects the bike chain from rust.

84370.q: Is rust still the same as iron?
a: No, it is a new substance
No, it is a kind of wood
No, it is a kind of garden soil
84370.e: When iron rusts, it combines with oxygen and water. This makes a completely new substance.

84371.q: On which metal can verdigris form?
84371.e: Verdigris is a green coating on copper. It also forms on metals that contain copper.

84372.q: What forms when copper is in contact with vinegar for a long time?
84372.e: The acid in vinegar attacks the copper. This creates a green coating called verdigris.

84373.q: Why must you never eat or lick verdigris?
84373.e: Verdigris is poisonous. That is why you should not keep food in copper pots with a green coating.

84374.q: What is the correct name for the green layer on old copper roofs?
84374.e: People often call it verdigris, but the correct name for this layer is patina. It forms slowly through air and rain.
84374.m: The green layer on copper roofs is called patina.

84375.q: Why is the green layer on a copper roof not removed?
84375.e: The green layer covers the copper like a coat. Underneath, the metal stays in good condition for many years.
84375.m: The green layer protects the copper roof.

84376.q: What did painters use verdigris for in the past?
84376.e: In the past, painters mixed a bright green paint from verdigris. Today there are non-poisonous paints for this.
84376.m: Verdigris used to be a paint.

84378.e: Brass contains copper. That is why a green coating can form on it too.
84378.m: Verdigris can also form on brass.

84379.q: What is kitchen foil used for?
84379.e: Kitchen foil can be wrapped tightly around food. That keeps it fresh or warm.
84379.m: You wrap food in kitchen foil.

84380.q: Can kitchen foil go in the microwave?
a: Yes, if it is completely smooth
Yes, if the food is cold
84380.e: Metal in the microwave can make sparks. That can damage the appliance or start a fire.
84380.m: Kitchen foil does not belong in the microwave.

84381.q: Which side of kitchen foil can you use?
84381.e: One side is dull only because of the way it is made. Both sides work almost equally well.
84381.m: You can use both sides of kitchen foil.

a: Thinner than a sheet of paper
84382.e: Kitchen foil is only about one hundredth of a millimetre thick. A sheet of paper is much thicker.
84382.m: Kitchen foil is thinner than paper.

84383.q: Why should you not wrap acidic food in kitchen foil?
84383.e: Acid from lemons or tomatoes attacks the foil. This can let aluminium get into the food.
84383.m: You do not wrap acidic food in kitchen foil.

84384.q: In which country did the first aluminium foil factory open in 1910?
84384.e: The first rolling mill for aluminium foil opened in 1910 in Kreuzlingen in the canton of Thurgau. From 1911 the foil also wrapped chocolate.
84384.m: The first aluminium foil was made in Switzerland.

84385.q: What do you do with clean, used kitchen foil in Switzerland?
a: Take it to the aluminium collection
Put it in the waste paper
Throw it in the bottle bank
84385.e: Aluminium can be melted down again and again. That is why clean foil is collected together with aluminium cans.
84385.m: Clean kitchen foil goes to the aluminium collection.

84386.q: What can you easily do with kitchen foil without any tools?
84386.e: Kitchen foil is very thin and soft. You can fold and shape it with your hands.
84386.m: Kitchen foil is easy to shape.

84387.q: What is a tin can for?
a: Keeping food for a long time
84387.e: In the sealed can, food stays good for a long time. No air and no germs can get in.
84387.m: A tin can keeps food for a long time.

84388.q: What do you use to open a tin without a ring pull?
84388.e: A tin opener cuts all the way round the lid. Then you can lift it off.
84388.m: You open tins with a tin opener.

84389.q: What is a tin can usually made of?
84389.e: Most tin cans are made of thin sheet steel. It is strong and protects the food well.
84389.m: Tin cans are usually made of sheet steel.

84390.q: Why does a tin can not rust so quickly?
a: It has a thin layer of tin
It is made of pure iron
84390.e: The sheet steel is covered with a fine layer of tin. This metal is called tinplate.
84390.m: A layer of tin protects tin cans from rust.

84391.q: What can you use to separate steel cans from aluminium cans?
84391.e: A magnet attracts steel but not aluminium. This makes the cans easy to sort.
84391.m: A magnet separates steel cans from aluminium cans.

84392.q: What does it mean if the lid of a tin bulges outwards?
a: The contents may have gone off
84392.e: When germs grow in the tin, they make gas. Then the lid bulges and you must not eat the contents.
84392.m: You throw away a bulging tin.

84393.q: What should you do with an empty tin before taking it to the collection point?
84393.e: Rinsed tins do not smell and do not attract animals. That way they can be recycled easily.
84393.m: You rinse empty tins before recycling them.

84394.q: Why is the food heated inside the sealed tin?
a: So that the tin gets lighter
84394.e: The heat kills the germs in the food. That is why the contents do not go off for so long.
84394.m: Heat kills the germs in the tin.

84395.q: How long does food usually stay good in a sealed tin?
84395.e: Tinned food often keeps for several years. The tin says until when the contents are at least good.
84395.m: Tinned food often keeps for several years.

84396.e: A smith heats metal in the fire until it glows. Then he shapes it with a hammer.

84397.q: What is a smith's workshop called?
84397.e: In the forge there is a fire, an anvil and lots of hammers. That is where the smith works.
84397.m: The smith works in the forge.

84398.q: On which heavy iron block does the smith hammer the metal?
84398.e: The anvil is a heavy block of steel. The smith lays the hot metal on it and hammers it into shape.
84398.m: The smith hammers the metal on the anvil.

84399.q: What does the smith use to hold the red-hot iron?
84399.e: The iron is far too hot to touch. With long tongs the smith holds it safely.
84399.m: The smith holds the hot iron with tongs.

84400.q: Why does the smith make the iron red-hot?
a: So it becomes soft and easy to shape
84400.e: Cold iron is hard and can hardly be shaped. Red-hot iron can be bent and stretched with a hammer.
84400.m: Red-hot iron is easy to shape.

84401.q: What is a smith who fits horseshoes on horses called?
84401.e: The farrier shapes horseshoes and fixes them to the horses' hooves. This protects the hooves.

84403.q: What does the smith use to blow air into the fire to make it hotter?
84403.e: The bellows pump air into the fire. More air makes the fire hotter.
84403.m: The smith makes the fire hotter with bellows.

84404.q: What is the smallest coin in Switzerland (as of 2026)?
84404.e: The 1-centime coin was withdrawn in 2007, and the 2-centime coin even earlier. Today the 5-centime coin is the smallest coin.
84404.m: The smallest Swiss coin is the 5-centime coin.

84405.q: What colour is the Swiss 5-centime coin?
84405.e: The 5-centime coin is made of a mixture containing copper and aluminium. That is why it shines golden yellow.

84406.q: Which female figure can be seen on Swiss 1-franc coins?
84406.e: Helvetia is a female figure who stands for Switzerland. She is shown standing with a spear and shield.

84407.q: In which city are Swiss coins made?
84407.e: The Swiss mint is called Swissmint. It is in Bern.
84407.m: Swiss coins are made in Bern.

84408.e: A machine presses the picture into a small metal disc with great force. This is called minting.

84409.q: What is the 5-franc coin often called in Switzerland?
84409.e: The 5-franc coin is the largest Swiss coin. In everyday life it is called the Fünfliber.
84409.m: The 5-franc coin is also called the Fünfliber.

84410.q: What are the two sides called when you toss a coin?
84410.e: One side shows the value, the number. The other side often shows a head or a picture.
84410.m: When you toss a coin, it is heads or tails.

84411.q: Which metals is the Swiss 1-franc coin made of?
84411.e: The shiny silver franc coins are made of copper and nickel. Until 1967 they were made of silver.
84411.m: The 1-franc coin is made of copper and nickel.

84412.q: What does a letter need so that the post office will send it?
84412.e: With the stamp you pay the post for the delivery. Without a stamp, the letter is not sent.

84413.q: What do you write on the front of an envelope?
84413.e: The address shows where the letter should go. That way the post knows who to bring it to.
84413.m: The address goes on the front of the letter.

84414.q: How many digits does a postcode have in Switzerland?
84414.e: Swiss postcodes have four digits, for example 3000 for Bern. They help with sorting the letters.

84415.q: Where do you put a stamped letter so that the post will collect it?
84415.e: Swiss Post’s yellow postboxes are emptied regularly. From there, the letters go to the sorting centre.
84415.m: You post letters in a Swiss Post postbox.

84416.q: What is the faster type of letter in Switzerland called?
84416.e: An A Post letter usually arrives the next working day. B Post is cheaper but takes longer.
84416.m: A Post is faster than B Post.

84417.e: On a postcard, the text is written openly on the card. On the other side there is often a picture.
84417.m: You send a postcard without an envelope.

84418.q: What do you often write at the top left of the envelope or on the back?
84418.e: The sender’s address is your own address. If the letter cannot be delivered, it comes back to you.
84418.m: The sender’s address belongs on the letter too.

84419.q: What did people use to write letters before there were ballpoint pens?
84419.e: In the past, people dipped a quill or a steel nib into ink. With it they wrote letter by letter.
84419.m: People used to write letters with pen and ink.

84420.q: What do you call a letter you send each other over the internet?
84420.e: An email is an electronic letter. It arrives in a few seconds.
84420.m: An email is a letter sent over the internet.

84421.q: In which country was the world’s first postage stamp issued in 1840?
84421.e: The first postage stamp was called the “Penny Black”. It was black and showed Queen Victoria.
84421.m: The first postage stamp came from Great Britain in 1840.

84422.q: Which Swiss canton was one of the first to issue postage stamps, in 1843?
84422.e: The “Zurich 4” and “Zurich 6” stamps are among the oldest in the world. Geneva followed in the same year.
84422.m: Zurich had postage stamps as early as 1843.

84423.q: What does the post office do to a stamp so it cannot be used again?
a: It sticks a second one on top
84423.e: The postmark shows that the stamp has already been used. That way it cannot be used a second time.

84424.q: Where do you stick the stamp on the envelope?
84424.e: The stamp goes at the top right on the front. That is where the machines find it when sorting.
84424.m: Stick the stamp at the top right.

84425.q: What do you call someone who collects stamps?
84425.e: Collecting stamps is called philately. Collectors keep their stamps in an album.
84425.m: A stamp collector is called a philatelist.

84426.q: What is the famous Basel stamp from 1845 called?
84426.e: The Basel Dove shows a white dove with a letter in its beak. It is one of the most beautiful old Swiss stamps.
84426.m: The Basel Dove is a famous stamp.

84427.q: What does the value on a Swiss stamp show?
84427.e: The stamp shows how many centimes or francs it is worth. That is how much you pay for sending.

84428.q: What can you write on a letter today instead of using a stamp?
a: A code from your mobile phone
84428.e: With Swiss Post, you can buy a code in the app. You write it on the letter by hand.
84428.m: Instead of a stamp you can write a code from the Post app.

84429.q: What are homing pigeons especially good at?
84429.e: Homing pigeons fly back to their loft even from far away. That is why they could be used as messengers.
84429.m: Homing pigeons find their way home.

84430.q: Where does a homing pigeon carry the message?
a: In a small tube on its leg
In a bag on its back
84430.e: The message is written on thin paper and rolled up. It goes into a small tube on the pigeon’s leg.
84430.m: Homing pigeons carry messages in a tube on their leg.

84431.q: What is the house where pigeons live called?
84431.e: The pigeon loft is the pigeons’ home. Homing pigeons always fly back there.
84431.m: Pigeons live in a pigeon loft.

84432.q: Until when did the Swiss Army have homing pigeons?
84432.e: The Swiss Army had a homing pigeon service from 1917 to 1994. Then it was disbanded.
84432.m: The Swiss Army had homing pigeons for a long time.

84433.q: Why were homing pigeons popular in wartime?
a: They need neither electricity nor cables
84433.e: A pigeon flies even when telephone lines are broken. That is why it was a good messenger in an emergency.
84433.m: Homing pigeons fly without electricity or cables.

84434.e: The pigeons are taken far away and released at the same time. The winner is the pigeon that gets home fastest.
84434.m: In a pigeon race, pigeons race each other home.

84435.q: In which direction can a homing pigeon carry a message?
84435.e: The pigeon only knows the way back to its loft. That is why it first had to be taken to the place the message came from.
84435.m: A homing pigeon always flies to its home.

84436.q: How can you tell who a homing pigeon belongs to?
a: By the ring on its leg
By the colour of its eyes
By the length of its beak
84436.e: Every homing pigeon wears a ring with a number. That way you know which breeder it belongs to.
84436.m: Homing pigeons wear a numbered ring.

84437.q: What do you need to make smoke signals?
84437.e: You make a fire with lots of smoke. With a blanket you interrupt the smoke and so make separate clouds.
84437.m: For smoke signals you need a fire and a blanket.

84438.q: Why do people make smoke signals on a hill?
a: So they can be seen from far away
So the smoke does not rise
84438.e: From a hill, the clouds of smoke can be seen over a long distance. Down in the valley, trees would hide them.
84438.m: Smoke signals are made in high places.

84439.q: When are smoke signals hard to see?
84439.e: In fog you cannot see the smoke. Smoke signals are also hard to see at night.
84439.m: Smoke signals are hard to see in fog.

84440.q: What colour is the smoke when a new pope has been elected in Rome?
84440.e: After each vote in the Vatican, smoke rises from a chimney. White smoke means there is a new pope.
84440.m: White smoke means a new pope has been elected.

84441.q: What were the signal fires on Swiss hills called in olden times?
84441.e: Watchmen stood ready at the beacon posts. When there was danger, they lit a fire, and the next beacon post passed the signal on.
84441.m: Beacon posts were old signal fires in Switzerland.

84442.q: What is a disadvantage of smoke signals?
a: You can only say a little
You can only hear them close by
You need a lot of water for them
You can only make them in winter
84442.e: With a few clouds of smoke you can only say simple things, for example “danger”. Long messages are not possible.
84442.m: Smoke signals can only send short messages.

84443.q: What were smoke and fire signals used for on the Great Wall of China?
84443.e: Watchmen stood on the towers of the wall. If they saw enemies, they raised the alarm with smoke and fire.
84443.m: On the Great Wall of China, smoke was used to warn of enemies.

84444.q: What does a smoke flare show today when someone is in distress at sea?
84444.e: On ships there are distress signals with coloured smoke. It shows rescuers where someone needs help.
84444.m: Coloured smoke at sea means distress.

84445.q: What signs make up Morse code?
84445.e: In Morse code, each letter is a series of short and long signals. They are written as dots and dashes.
84445.m: Morse code is made of dots and dashes.

84446.q: Which well-known distress call is sent in Morse code?
84446.e: SOS is the best-known distress call. It is easy to send and to recognise.
84446.m: SOS is a distress call in Morse code.

84447.q: How is SOS sent in Morse code?
a: Three short, three long, three short
Three long, three short, three long
84447.e: S is three short and O is three long. So you get short, short, short, long, long, long, short, short, short.
84447.m: SOS is three short, three long, three short.

84448.q: What can you use to send Morse code?
84448.e: You can beep, knock or flash Morse code with a lamp. All that matters is short and long.
84448.m: You can send Morse code with light or sound.

84449.q: Which letter is just a single short dot in Morse code?
84449.e: The letter E is the most common letter in English. That is why it was given the shortest signal.
84449.m: In Morse code, E is a single dot.

84450.q: Which device was used in the past to send Morse code over wires?
84450.e: The telegraph sent short and long pulses of electricity down a wire. At the other end they were translated back into letters.
84450.m: Morse code was sent with the telegraph.

84451.q: What is the key you use to send Morse code called?
84451.e: Press the Morse key briefly and you get a dot. Hold it longer and you get a dash.
84451.m: You send Morse code with the Morse key.

84452.q: Which letter is a single long dash in Morse code?
84452.e: T is a single dash. M is two dashes and O is three dashes.
84452.m: In Morse code, T is a single dash.

84453.q: Who still uses Morse code as a hobby today?
84453.e: Radio amateurs send each other messages by radio in their free time. Many of them can still use Morse code.
84453.m: Radio amateurs still use Morse code today.

84454.q: What do you call a small radio you hold in your hand?
84454.e: With a walkie-talkie you can talk to someone nearby without a cable. Both people need a device.
84454.m: A walkie-talkie is a small radio.

84455.q: What must you press on a radio when you want to speak?
84455.e: As long as you press the push-to-talk button, the device transmits. When you let go, you can listen again.
84455.m: To speak, press the push-to-talk button.

84456.q: How does your voice get from one radio to the other?
a: Through the air on radio waves
84456.e: The radio turns your voice into invisible radio waves. The other device picks them up and turns them back into sound.

84457.q: On a simple radio, can both people talk at the same time?
a: No, only one after the other
Yes, but only in the evening
84457.e: On a simple radio, only one person talks at a time. That is why you say “Over” at the end, so the other person knows it is their turn.
84457.m: On the radio, only one person talks at a time.

84458.q: Who often uses radios at work?
84458.e: The police and fire brigade have to coordinate quickly on call-outs. With radios that works even without a mobile network.
84458.m: The police and fire brigade use radios.

84459.q: Which part of the radio sends and receives the radio waves?
84459.e: The aerial sends out the radio waves and picks them up. It is often a small rod at the top of the device.
84459.m: The aerial sends and receives radio waves.

84460.q: What must be set the same on both radios?
84460.e: Radios transmit on different channels. Only when both are on the same channel can they hear each other.
84460.m: Both radios need the same channel.

84461.q: Which word do you call on the radio when an aircraft or ship is in grave danger?
84461.e: Mayday is the distress call in radio speech. You call it three times in a row.
84461.m: Mayday is the distress call on the radio.

84462.e: A telegram was sent over wires and written down at its destination. A messenger then took it quickly to the recipient.
84462.m: A telegram was a fast, short message.

84463.q: Why did people use as few words as possible in telegrams?
84463.e: Every word in a telegram cost money. That is why people kept it very short.
84463.m: In telegrams, every word cost money.

84464.q: Which English word was often used instead of a full stop in telegrams?
84464.e: Punctuation marks were hard to send. That is why people wrote the word STOP where a sentence ended.
84464.m: In telegrams, STOP replaced the full stop.

84465.q: Who brought the telegram to the recipient’s home?
84465.e: The telegram was printed out at the telegraph office. A messenger took it to the address as fast as possible.
84465.m: A telegram messenger delivered the telegram.

84466.q: How did a telegram’s message travel from city to city?
84466.e: The message was sent through wires as electrical signals. That was much faster than a letter.

84467.q: For which occasion did people often send a congratulations telegram in the past?
84467.e: Anyone who could not come to the wedding sent a telegram. It contained short good wishes.
84467.m: People often sent congratulations telegrams for weddings.

84468.q: What has mostly replaced the telegram today?
84468.e: Today people send each other text messages on their phones. They arrive in seconds and cost almost nothing.
84468.m: Text messages have replaced the telegram.

84469.q: Where could you send a telegram in the past?
84469.e: You wrote the text on a form and handed it in at the post office counter. The post office then sent the message on.
84469.m: Telegrams were sent from the post office.

84470.q: What does a mobile phone need so you can make calls with it?
84470.e: The SIM card connects the phone to the provider’s network. Without it you normally cannot make calls.
84470.m: A mobile phone needs a SIM card.

84471.q: Which number do you dial on a mobile phone in an emergency anywhere in Europe?
84471.e: The number 112 works in all EU countries and in Switzerland. You are put through to the emergency centre.

84472.q: What do you use to take photos with a mobile phone?
84472.e: Almost every phone has a built-in camera. With it you can take photos and videos.
84472.m: The phone takes photos with its camera.

84473.q: Which part of the phone do you need so the other person can hear your voice?
84473.e: The microphone picks up your voice. The phone then sends it to the other phone.
84473.m: The microphone picks up your voice.

84474.q: How do you send a short written message with a mobile phone?
a: You type it in and send it
You shout it into the phone
You stick a note on it
84474.e: You type the message on the screen. Then you press send.
84474.m: You type text messages in and send them.

84475.q: What did the first mobile phones look like?
84475.e: The first mobile phones were as big as a brick. That is why German speakers nicknamed them ‘bones’.
84475.m: The first mobile phones were big and heavy.

84476.q: What do the bars at the top of the phone screen show?
84476.e: Lots of bars mean a good signal. With only a few bars, a call can drop.

84477.q: What should you do with your mobile phone in the cinema?
84477.e: A ringing phone disturbs the other people watching. That is why you put it on silent or switch it off.
84477.m: In the cinema, put your phone on silent.

84478.q: Why should you not look at your phone while cycling?
84478.e: If you look at your phone, you are not watching the road. That is how accidents quickly happen.
84478.m: When cycling, keep your phone in your pocket.

a: A phone with a cable to a line in the house
A mobile phone for your pocket
A radio for on the go
A bell at the front door
84479.e: The landline phone is connected to a line in the wall. That is why you cannot take it everywhere.
84479.m: A landline phone is connected to a line in the house.

84480.q: What did you use to dial the number on old telephones?
84480.e: You put your finger in a hole of the dial and turned it. Then the dial ran back and the digit was dialled.
84480.m: Old telephones had a rotary dial.

84481.q: What is the part of the telephone you hold to your ear called?
84481.e: The receiver contains a small loudspeaker and a microphone. You pick it up to make a call.
84481.m: You hold the receiver to your ear.

84482.q: Which number do you dial in Switzerland for the fire brigade?
84482.e: You reach the fire brigade on 118. The police are on 117 and the ambulance service on 144.
84482.m: You reach the fire brigade on 118.

84483.q: What was the little booth where you could make calls when out and about called?
84483.e: In the past there were lots of phone boxes in streets and at stations. You paid with coins or a phonecard.
84483.m: In the past, people made calls from phone boxes when out and about.

84484.q: In which thick book were telephone numbers listed in the past?
84484.e: The phone book listed people’s names with their number and address. That way you could look numbers up.
84484.m: Phone numbers used to be listed in the phone book.

84485.q: What do you hear when you pick up the receiver and the line is free?
84485.e: The dialling tone shows that you can dial. If the line is engaged, on the other hand, you hear short beeps.
84485.m: The dialling tone shows you can dial.

84486.q: What does the area code 031 on a Swiss landline number show?
84486.e: Area codes show which region a landline connection is from. 031 belongs to Bern, and 044 to Zurich, for example.
84486.m: The area code 031 belongs to Bern.

84487.q: What else can you do in a video call besides hearing each other?
84487.e: In a video call, the camera films your face. The other person sees it on their screen.
84487.m: In a video call you see each other.

84488.q: What does a device absolutely need for a video call?
84488.e: Without a camera, the device cannot send a picture of you. That is why phones, tablets and laptops have a built-in camera.
84488.m: You need a camera for video calls.

84489.q: What do you need for a video call using an app?
84489.e: Picture and sound are sent over the internet. Without internet, the video call does not work.

84490.q: What happens in a video call if the internet is too slow?
84490.e: Pictures need a lot of data to be sent. If the internet is slow, it does not arrive in time.
84490.m: With slow internet, the picture stutters.

84491.q: What do many families use video calls for?
a: To see relatives who live far away
84491.e: This way you can see and hear grandparents or relatives abroad. It is almost like a visit.
84491.m: With video calls you see relatives who live far away.

84492.q: What do you call a telephone that lets you see the other person too?
84492.e: People dreamed of the videophone many decades ago. Today almost every mobile phone can do it.
84492.m: The videophone was an old dream.

84493.q: What should you keep in mind with video calls?
a: Only show yourself to people you know
Talk to strangers for a long time
84493.e: In a video, people see a lot of you and your home. That is why you only make video calls with people you know.
84493.m: Only make video calls with people you know.

84494.q: How can you switch off your own microphone in a video conference?
84494.e: With the mute button, nobody can hear you. That way you do not disturb anyone while someone else is talking.
84494.m: The mute button switches off your microphone.

84496.q: Where does the postman put the letters?
84496.e: Every house has a letterbox with the residents’ names. The postman puts the post in there.

84497.q: What must be written on the letterbox so the post arrives correctly?
84497.e: The postman looks at the name on the letterbox. That way he knows whose post is whose.
84497.m: The name must be on the letterbox.

84498.e: You can recognise Swiss Post by its yellow colour. The postboxes and vehicles are yellow too.

84499.q: What do postmen in Switzerland often ride through neighbourhoods?
84499.e: Many postmen ride yellow three-wheeled electric scooters. They have room on them for letters and small parcels.

84500.q: What does the postman put in the letterbox if a parcel could not be delivered?
84500.e: The note says where you can collect the parcel. Usually that is the nearest post office.
84500.m: With the collection notice you collect the parcel from the post office.

84501.q: On which day of the week does the postman in Switzerland normally not bring letters?
84501.e: During the week, the postman brings the post. On Sunday he has the day off, so no letters come.
84501.m: No letters are delivered on Sunday.

84502.q: What did the postman often carry over his shoulder in the past?
84502.e: The postman carried letters and newspapers in the big leather bag. He went from house to house on foot with it.
84502.m: The postman used to carry a postbag.

84503.q: Where are the many letters sorted before the postman delivers them?
84503.e: At the sorting centre, machines read the addresses and sort the letters. Then the postmen get the post for their round.
84503.m: Letters are sorted at the sorting centre.

84504.q: What do you need a satellite dish on a house for?
84504.e: The dish picks up signals from satellites in space. That way you can receive lots of TV channels.
84504.m: The satellite dish receives television from space.

84505.q: What shape is a satellite dish?
84505.e: The curved bowl collects the signals like a funnel. The receiver sits in front of the middle.
84505.m: A satellite dish is shaped like a bowl.

84506.q: Where is the satellite that the dish receives signals from?
a: High above the Earth in space
84506.e: TV satellites orbit far out in space. From there, their signals reach the whole of Europe.
84506.m: The TV satellite is in space.

84507.q: Which direction do satellite dishes in Switzerland point?
84507.e: TV satellites are high above the equator. Seen from Switzerland, the equator lies to the south.
84507.m: In Switzerland, satellite dishes point south.

84508.q: Why must nothing stand in front of the satellite dish?
a: Otherwise the signal does not get through
84508.e: Trees or walls can block the signals. The dish needs a clear view of the satellite.
84508.m: A satellite dish needs a clear view.

84509.q: What sometimes disturbs a satellite dish’s reception?
84509.e: Thick rain clouds or snow on the dish weaken the signal. Then the picture can drop out briefly.
84509.m: Heavy rain can disturb satellite reception.

84510.q: Which huge dishes stand in Leuk in Valais?
84510.e: In Leuk there are large dish aerials for satellite links. They can be seen clearly from far away.
84510.m: There are large satellite aerials in Leuk.

84511.q: What does the small head in front of the dish do?
a: It picks up the collected signals
84511.e: The dish reflects the signals to a point in front of it. That is where the receiving head sits, passing them on to the TV.
84511.m: The receiving head picks up the signals.

84512.q: Lea gets 25 francs pocket money a month. How much money does she get in a year?
84512.e: A year has 12 months. 12 · 25 francs makes 300 francs.
84512.m: For the yearly amount, you multiply the monthly amount by 12.

84513.q: Tim gets 6 francs a week and saves half of it each time. How much has he saved after 8 weeks?
84513.e: Half of 6 francs is 3 francs. 8 · 3 francs makes 24 francs.
84513.m: If you regularly save a fixed amount, you reach your goal step by step.

84514.q: Mia wants to buy headphones for 72 francs and puts aside 8 francs every week. How many weeks does she have to save?
84514.e: You divide the price by the amount saved per week: 72 : 8 makes 9 weeks.
84514.m: You find the saving time by dividing the price by the amount saved.

84515.q: Noah has 40 francs and spends 15 per cent of it on a comic. How much does the comic cost?
84515.e: 10 per cent of 40 francs is 4 francs, 5 per cent is 2 francs. Together that makes 6 francs.
84515.m: You can often split percentages into easy parts like 10 per cent and 5 per cent.

84516.q: Sara has 30 francs pocket money. She saves 12 francs and spends 9 francs at the cinema. What percentage of her pocket money is left?
84516.e: What is left is 30 − 12 − 9, which makes 9 francs. 9 out of 30 francs is 9 : 30, which makes 0.3, so 30 per cent.
84516.m: You get a share as a percentage by dividing the part by the whole.

84517.q: Jan has 50 francs and spends 7.50 francs every week. After how many weeks does he first have less than 10 francs?
84517.e: After 5 weeks, 50 − 37.50 leaves 12.50 francs. After 6 weeks, 50 − 45 leaves 5 francs, which is less than 10 francs.
84517.m: With regular spending, it is worth tracking your balance week by week.

84518.q: Luca gets 20 francs a month. After his birthday he gets 25 per cent more. How much pocket money does he get now?
84518.e: 25 per cent of 20 francs is a quarter, so 5 francs. 20 + 5 makes 25 francs.
84518.m: An increase of 25 per cent means a quarter is added.

84519.q: In one month, Elin took in 35 francs and spent 28.40 francs. How much money does she have left?
84519.e: You work out income minus spending: 35.00 − 28.40 makes 6.60 francs.
84519.m: You work out what is left as income minus spending.

84520.q: What does the unit price on a price label show?
a: The price for a fixed amount such as 1 kg
The lowest price in the whole shop
The price before a special offer
84520.e: The unit price converts the price to a unit such as 1 kilogram, 1 litre or 100 grams. That way you can compare packs of different sizes.
84520.m: The unit price lets you compare packs of different sizes fairly.

84521.q: A 500 g pack of pasta costs 2.40 francs. What is the unit price per kilogram?
84521.e: 1 kg is 1000 g, so twice as much as 500 g. 2 · 2.40 francs makes 4.80 francs.
84521.m: For a 500 g pack, the price per kilogram is twice the pack price.

84522.q: 250 g of butter costs 3.50 francs. How much does 1 kg of butter cost at the same unit price?
84522.e: 1 kg is four times 250 g. 4 · 3.50 francs makes 14.00 francs.
84522.m: If you know the unit price, you know what a whole unit would cost.

84523.q: A 1.5-litre bottle of mineral water costs 0.90 francs. What is the price per litre?
84523.e: You divide the price by the amount: 0.90 : 1.5 makes 0.60 francs per litre.
84523.m: You get the price per litre by dividing the price by the number of litres.

84524.q: Rice comes in two packs: 400 g for 3.20 francs or 750 g for 5.70 francs. Which pack has the lower unit price?
84524.e: The small pack costs 3.20 : 0.4, which makes 8.00 francs per kg. The big one costs 5.70 : 0.75, which makes 7.60 francs per kg.
84524.m: Only comparing the unit prices shows which pack is really cheaper.

84525.q: A 180 g yoghurt costs 0.90 francs. How much do 100 g cost?
84525.e: Per gram the yoghurt costs 0.90 : 180, which makes 0.005 francs. For 100 g that is 0.50 francs.
84525.m: For small packs, the unit price is often given per 100 grams.

84526.q: Where do you find the unit price of a product in a shop?
a: On the price label by the product
84526.e: In Switzerland, the unit price must also be shown for packaged goods. It is usually in small print on the price label on the shelf.
84526.m: The unit price is on the price label.

84527.q: A 300 ml shampoo costs 4.50 francs. How much would 1 litre cost at the same unit price?
84527.e: 100 ml cost 4.50 : 3, which makes 1.50 francs. 1 litre is 1000 ml, so 10 · 1.50 makes 15.00 francs.
84527.m: Using the price for 100 ml, you can easily work out the price per litre.

84528.q: What does an exchange rate tell you?
a: How much one currency is worth in another
How much interest a bank pays
How much a bank account costs per year
How many coins a country mints
84528.e: The exchange rate is the price of one currency in another currency. It shows, for example, how many francs you pay for one euro.
84528.m: The exchange rate is the price of one currency expressed in another.

84529.q: Suppose 1 euro costs 0.95 francs. How many francs do you pay for 40 euros?
84529.e: You multiply the number of euros by the rate: 40 · 0.95 makes 38 francs.
84529.m: To convert euros into francs, you multiply by the rate.

84530.q: Suppose you get 1.05 euros for 1 franc. How many euros do you get for 200 francs?
84530.e: 200 · 1.05 makes 210 euros. So you get a few more euros than francs.
84530.m: If the franc is worth more than the euro, you get more euros for your francs.

84531.q: Which currency do you pay with on holiday in Austria?
84531.e: Austria is part of the eurozone and has paid with euro cash since 2002. The schilling was replaced then.
84531.m: In Austria you pay with the euro.

84532.q: Which code stands for the Swiss franc in international payments?
84532.e: The international currency code of the Swiss franc is CHF. CH stands for Confoederatio Helvetica, F for franc.
84532.m: The Swiss franc has the currency code CHF.

84533.q: Suppose 1 US dollar costs 0.80 francs. How many francs does a T-shirt for 25 dollars cost?
84533.e: 25 · 0.80 makes 20 francs. Because a dollar costs less than a franc here, the amount in francs is smaller.
84533.m: If a foreign unit costs less than a franc, the amount in francs is smaller.

84534.q: After your holiday you change 50 euros back. The bank pays you 0.90 francs per euro. How many francs do you get?
84534.e: 50 · 0.90 makes 45 francs. When changing money back, you usually get a slightly worse rate than when buying.
84534.m: Banks buy back foreign currencies at a lower rate than they sell them.

84535.q: The franc becomes stronger against the euro. What does that mean for holidays in the eurozone?
a: They become cheaper for Swiss people
They become more expensive for Swiss people
84535.e: A strong franc means you get more euros for one franc. So goods priced in euros cost fewer francs when converted.
84535.m: A strong franc makes shopping abroad cheaper for Swiss people.

84536.q: Suppose you get 170 Japanese yen for 1 franc. How many yen does an ice cream cost that comes to 3 francs?
84536.e: 3 · 170 makes 510 yen. The yen is worth much less than the franc, so the numbers are big.
84536.m: With currencies of low value, price labels show big numbers.

84537.q: Which time zone applies in Switzerland in winter?
84537.e: Switzerland is in the Central European Time zone, CET for short. In summer, Central European Summer Time applies.
84537.m: In winter, Switzerland uses Central European Time.

84538.q: By how many hours is Central European Time (CET) ahead of Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)?
84538.e: CET is UTC+1. If it is 11 o’clock UTC, it is 12 o’clock in Switzerland in winter.
84538.m: Central European Time is one hour ahead of UTC.

84539.q: By how much is the clock changed in Switzerland when summer time starts?
84539.e: In spring, the clock goes forward one hour, for example from 2 o’clock to 3 o’clock. In autumn it goes back again.
84539.m: In spring the clocks go forward an hour, in autumn back an hour.

84540.q: In winter, it is one hour earlier in London than in Zurich. What time is it in London when it is 15.00 in Zurich?
84540.e: London is in the UTC+0 zone, Zurich in winter in UTC+1. So 15 − 1 makes 14.00.
84540.m: West of Switzerland it is often earlier, east of it later.

84541.q: Tokyo is in the UTC+9 zone, Zurich in winter in UTC+1. What time is it in Tokyo when it is 10.00 in Zurich?
84541.e: The difference is 9 − 1, which makes 8 hours. 10 + 8 makes 18.00 in Tokyo.
84541.m: You find the time difference as the difference between the two UTC offsets.

84542.q: In winter, New York is in the UTC−5 zone and Zurich in UTC+1. What time is it in New York when it is 18.00 in Zurich?
84542.e: The difference is 1 − (−5), which makes 6 hours. 18 − 6 makes 12.00 in New York.
84542.m: On the east coast of the USA it is usually six hours earlier than in Switzerland.

84543.q: A flight leaves Zurich at 13.00 local time and takes 9 hours. At the destination it is 6 hours earlier than in Zurich. When does the plane land in local time?
84543.e: In Zurich time, the plane lands at 13 + 9, which makes 22.00. At the destination it is 6 hours earlier, so 16.00.
84543.m: With flight times, you first work in the departure time and then subtract the time difference.

84544.q: By how many degrees of longitude does the Earth turn in one hour?
84544.e: The Earth turns 360 degrees in 24 hours. 360 : 24 makes 15 degrees per hour, which is why a time zone is roughly 15 degrees of longitude wide.
84544.m: A time zone is roughly 15 degrees of longitude wide.

84545.q: A car uses 6 litres of petrol per 100 km. How much petrol does it need for 250 km?
84545.e: 250 km is 2.5 times 100 km. 2.5 · 6 litres makes 15 litres.
84545.m: You work out the fuel for a journey from the consumption per 100 km.

84546.q: A car needs exactly 32 litres of diesel for 400 km. What is its consumption per 100 km?
84546.e: 32 litres spread over 4 times 100 km gives 32 : 4, which makes 8 litres per 100 km.
84546.m: If you divide the litres used by the distance in hundreds of kilometres, you get the consumption.

84547.q: A tank holds 50 litres and the car uses 5 litres per 100 km. How far can it go on a full tank?
84547.e: With 5 litres it goes 100 km. 50 litres is ten times as much, so 10 · 100 makes 1000 km.
84547.m: The range depends on the tank size and the consumption.

84548.q: A car uses 7 litres per 100 km, and a litre of petrol costs 1.90 francs. How much does the petrol for 300 km cost?
84548.e: For 300 km the car needs 3 · 7, which makes 21 litres. 21 · 1.90 makes 39.90 francs.
84548.m: You get the cost of a journey from the consumption times the price per litre.

84549.q: In which unit is a car’s fuel consumption usually given in Switzerland?
84549.e: In Europe and Switzerland, people state how many litres a car needs for 100 km. In the USA, on the other hand, they use miles per gallon.
84549.m: In Switzerland, consumption is given in litres per 100 kilometres.

84550.q: In which unit is the energy consumption of an electric car usually given?
84550.e: An electric car needs electrical energy, which is measured in kilowatt hours. Typical figures are around 16 kWh per 100 km.
84550.m: The consumption of an electric car is measured in kilowatt hours per 100 kilometres.

84551.q: The Meier family drives 90 km to a day-trip destination and 90 km back. Their car uses 6 litres per 100 km. How much petrol do they need altogether?
84551.e: The whole distance is 180 km, so 1.8 times 100 km. 1.8 · 6 makes 10.8 litres.
84551.m: On day trips, do not forget the return journey in your calculation.

84552.q: A family drives 12,000 km a year in a car that uses 6.5 litres per 100 km. How many litres of petrol do they use a year?
84552.e: 12,000 km is 120 times 100 km. 120 · 6.5 makes 780 litres.
84552.m: Even small differences in consumption add up to many litres over a year.

84553.q: A streaming subscription costs 12.90 francs a month. How much does it cost in a year?
84553.e: 12 · 12.90 francs makes 154.80 francs. Small monthly amounts add up to a large sum over a year.
84553.m: You should always work out monthly subscription costs for the whole year too.

84554.q: A subscription costs 12 francs monthly or 120 francs as an annual subscription. How much do you save with the annual subscription?
84554.e: Paid monthly, the subscription costs 12 · 12, which makes 144 francs a year. 144 − 120 makes a saving of 24 francs.
84554.m: Annual subscriptions are often cheaper but tie you in for longer.

84555.q: Mobile plan A costs 30 francs a month for unlimited calls. Plan B costs 10 francs plus 0.50 francs per minute. From how many minutes a month is plan A cheaper?
84555.e: With 40 minutes, plan B costs 10 + 40 · 0.50, which makes 30 francs, the same as A. With more minutes, B gets more expensive.
84555.m: When comparing plans, you look for the point where both offers cost the same.

84556.q: Entry to the swimming pool costs 8 francs, a season ticket 96 francs. At how many visits do both options cost the same?
84556.e: 96 : 8 makes 12. Anyone who goes more than twelve times saves with the season ticket.
84556.m: A season ticket is only worth it if you use it often enough.

84557.q: Suppose a Half Fare travelcard costs 190 francs. A ticket normally costs 38 francs, with the Half Fare travelcard half that. After how many journeys has the travelcard paid for itself?
84557.e: Per journey you save 38 : 2, which makes 19 francs. 190 : 19 makes 10 journeys.
84557.m: Dividing the card price by the saving per journey tells you when the card pays off.

84558.q: What does a notice period of three months mean for a subscription?
a: The subscription only ends three months after you cancel
You may only cancel after three months
The first three months are free
You must pay three months in advance
84558.e: A notice period is the time between cancelling and the end of the contract. During this time you still have to pay for the subscription.
84558.m: If you want to end a subscription, plan the notice period in good time.

84559.q: A subscription is free for the first three months and then costs 9.90 francs a month. How much does it cost in the first year?
84559.e: You pay for 12 − 3, which makes 9 months. 9 · 9.90 makes 89.10 francs.
84559.m: Free months only lower the cost at the start; after that the subscription runs as normal.

84560.q: A magazine comes out 12 times a year and costs 6 francs per issue. The annual subscription costs 54 francs. What percentage do you save with the subscription?
84560.e: Bought singly, 12 issues cost 72 francs. You save 72 − 54, which makes 18 francs, and 18 : 72 makes 0.25, so 25 per cent.
84560.m: A saving in per cent always refers to the original price.

84561.q: Someone borrows 600 francs at an interest rate of 5 per cent a year. How much interest do they have to pay after one year?
84561.e: 5 per cent of 600 francs is 600 · 0.05, which makes 30 francs. If you borrow money, you have to pay interest on it.
84561.m: With a loan, too, you work out yearly interest as capital times interest rate divided by 100.

84562.q: How much interest do 1200 francs earn in one year at an interest rate of 1.5 per cent?
84562.e: 1 per cent of 1200 francs is 12 francs, 0.5 per cent is 6 francs. Together that makes 18 francs.
84562.m: You can split an interest rate with a decimal point into whole and half per cents.

84563.q: Someone invests 800 francs at 2 per cent and takes out the interest every year. How much interest do they get in three years altogether?
84563.e: Each year there are 800 · 0.02, which makes 16 francs. With simple interest, three years make 3 · 16, which is 48 francs.
84563.m: With simple interest, the interest is the same every year.

84564.q: Capital of 1000 francs earns 30 francs interest in one year. What is the interest rate?
84564.m: You get the interest rate by dividing the interest by the capital.

84565.q: At an interest rate of 4 per cent, someone gets 20 francs interest in one year. How big is the capital?
84565.e: 4 per cent equals 20 francs, so 1 per cent is 5 francs. 100 per cent is 500 francs.
84565.m: If you know the interest and the interest rate, you find the capital with the unitary method.

84566.q: How much interest do 2000 francs at 3 per cent a year earn in half a year?
84566.e: In a whole year there would be 2000 · 0.03, which makes 60 francs. In half a year it is half, so 30 francs.
84566.m: For parts of a year, you work out the yearly interest proportionally.

84567.q: A recipe for 4 people needs 200 g of flour. How much flour is needed for 6 people?
84567.e: For 1 person it is 200 : 4, which makes 50 g. For 6 people 6 · 50 makes 300 g.
84567.m: When converting recipes, you first work it out for one person.

84568.q: For a cake for 4 people you need 3 eggs. How many eggs do you need for 8 people?
84568.e: 8 people is twice as many as 4. So you need 2 · 3, which makes 6 eggs.
84568.m: If you double the number of people, all the ingredients double.

84569.q: A recipe for 6 people needs 900 g of potatoes. How much is needed for 2 people?
84569.e: 2 people is a third of 6 people. 900 : 3 makes 300 g.
84569.m: For fewer people, you divide all the amounts in the same ratio.

84570.e: A litre has 10 decilitres and 1000 millilitres. So a decilitre is 1000 : 10, which makes 100 ml.
84570.m: A decilitre equals a hundred millilitres.

84571.q: A recipe for 4 people needs 1.2 litres of milk. How much milk is needed for 3 people?
84571.e: For 1 person it is 1.2 : 4, which makes 0.3 litres. For 3 people 3 · 0.3 makes 0.9 litres, so 9 dl.
84571.m: In Swiss recipes, liquids are often given in decilitres.

84573.q: A recipe for 12 biscuits needs 150 g of butter. How much butter do you need for 30 biscuits?
84573.e: For 1 biscuit you need 150 : 12, which makes 12.5 g. For 30 biscuits 30 · 12.5 makes 375 g.
84573.m: The unitary method also helps with awkward amounts in recipes.

84574.q: A recipe for 4 people needs 3/4 litre of cream. How much cream do you need for 2 people?
84574.e: Half of 3/4 litre is 3/8 litre. 3/8 litre is 0.375 litres, so 3.75 dl.
84574.m: You can turn fractions in recipes into decimals to make calculating easier.

84575.q: What is the method called that you use to convert the amounts in a recipe to a different number of people?
84575.e: With the unitary method, you first work out the amount for one unit, for example one person, and then for the number you want. That way you can convert proportional amounts.
84575.m: With the unitary method, you go via one unit to the amount you want.

84576.q: Mara has the marks 5, 4.5 and 5.5. What is her average?
84576.e: The sum is 5 + 4.5 + 5.5, which makes 15. Divided by 3 marks that makes 5.
84576.m: You get the average from the sum divided by the number of values.

84577.q: Which mark is the best in most Swiss schools?
84577.e: In Switzerland, the marking scale usually goes from 1 to 6. 6 is the best mark, 1 the worst.
84577.m: In Switzerland, 6 is the best school mark.

84578.q: From which mark does work count as a pass in Switzerland?
84578.e: On the Swiss scale from 1 to 6, 4 is the lowest pass mark. Marks below 4 are a fail.
84578.m: In Switzerland, the mark 4 is the pass mark.

84579.q: Leo has a test with the mark 4 and an exam with the mark 5. The exam counts double. What is his average?
84579.e: You work out (4 + 2 · 5) : 3, which makes 14 : 3, so about 4.67. The mark that counts double is added twice.
84579.m: With weighted marks, an important mark counts several times.

84580.q: Ana has the marks 4.5 and 5. Which mark does she need in the third exam for an average of exactly 5?
84580.e: For an average of 5 with 3 marks she needs a sum of 15. 15 − 4.5 − 5 makes 5.5.
84580.m: From the average you want, you can work out the total of marks you need.

84581.q: An average of 4.7 is rounded to the nearest half mark. Which mark do you get?
84581.e: 4.7 is 0.2 away from 4.5 and 0.3 away from 5. So it is rounded to 4.5.
84581.m: When rounding to half marks, you choose the nearest half mark.

84582.q: What is the median of the marks 2, 5, 5.5, 6 and 6?
84582.e: The median is the value in the middle of the ordered list. With five marks it is the third, so 5.5; the average would be 4.9.
84582.m: The median is the middle value of an ordered list.

84583.q: A pupil has 4 marks with an average of 4.5. What is the sum of these marks?
84583.e: Average times number gives the sum: 4.5 · 4 makes 18.
84583.m: If you know the average and the number, you can work back to the sum.

84584.q: Tom has the marks 4, 5 and 6. Then he gets a 3. What is his average with all four marks?
84584.e: The sum is 4 + 5 + 6 + 3, which makes 18. Divided by 4 marks that makes 4.5.
84584.m: A bad mark pulls the average down.

84585.q: A football team has 7 wins and 25 points altogether. How many draws has it played?
84585.e: The wins bring 7 · 3, which makes 21 points. The remaining 25 − 21, which makes 4 points, come from draws worth 1 point each.
84585.m: From points and wins you can work back to the number of draws.

84586.q: A football team has 5 wins, 3 draws and 2 defeats. How many points does it have?
84586.e: The wins give 5 · 3, which makes 15 points, the draws 3 · 1, which makes 3 points. Together that makes 18 points.
84586.m: The points total is wins times three plus draws.

84587.q: A team has scored 25 goals and conceded 18. What is the goal difference?
84587.e: The goal difference is goals scored minus goals conceded: 25 − 18 makes +7.
84587.m: A positive goal difference shows that a team scores more goals than it concedes.

84588.q: In a group of 4 teams, each team plays every other team exactly once. How many matches are there altogether?
84588.e: Each team has 3 opponents, which gives 4 · 3, so 12 pairings. Each match has been counted twice, so 12 : 2 makes 6 matches.
84588.m: With “everyone against everyone”, you must not count any match twice.

84589.q: How many teams play in the Swiss Super League in the 2025/26 season?
84589.e: From the 2023/24 season, the Super League was expanded from 10 to 12 teams. In 2025/26, 12 teams play too.
84589.m: Twelve teams play in the Swiss Super League (as of 2025).

84590.q: In the Swiss ice hockey championship, the National League, how many points does a team get if it only loses after overtime or a penalty shootout?
84590.e: A win after 60 minutes gives 3 points. If a game goes to overtime, the winner gets 2 points and the loser 1 point.
84590.m: In ice hockey, even the loser after overtime still gets a point.

84591.q: After 15 matches, a team has 30 points. How many points has it won on average per match?
84591.e: 30 : 15 makes 2 points per match. This figure shows how strong a team is, even if it has played fewer matches.
84591.m: Points per match make teams with different numbers of matches comparable.

84592.q: In a league of 10 teams, each team plays every other team once at home and once away. How many matches does a team play?
84592.e: Each team has 9 opponents. It plays each of them twice, so 2 · 9 makes 18 matches.
84592.m: In a league with home and away rounds, you play every opponent twice.

84593.q: What does the key (legend) of a chart explain?
a: What the colours and symbols mean
84593.e: The key shows which colour or symbol stands for which data series. Without a key, many charts cannot be read properly.
84593.m: The key tells you what the colours in a chart stand for.

84598.q: In a survey of 200 people, 35 per cent say “Yes”. How many people is that?
84598.e: 35 per cent of 200 is 200 · 0.35, which makes 70 people.
84598.m: Behind percentages in charts there are always real numbers.

84599.q: In a pictogram, one figure stands for 10 people. How many people do 4.5 figures mean?
84599.e: Each whole figure stands for 10 people, a half for 5. So 4.5 · 10 makes 45 people.
84599.m: In pictograms, you first have to check how much one symbol means.

84600.q: A bar chart shows 40 girls and 60 boys at a school. What is the share of girls?
84600.e: Altogether there are 40 + 60, which makes 100 children. 40 out of 100 is 40 per cent.
84600.m: For a share, you divide the subgroup by the total.

a: A price reduction for buying larger quantities
A discount only for regular customers
A price reduction for paying in cash
84601.e: With a bulk discount, people who buy more pay less per item. Shops use it to make bigger sales.
84601.m: With a bulk discount, the price per item falls when you buy more.

84602.q: In a “3 for 2” offer, one item costs 1.50 francs on its own. What percentage do you save if you buy three?
84602.e: You only pay for 2 of the 3 items, so 3.00 instead of 4.50 francs. 1.50 ÷ 4.50 is one third, which is about 33 per cent.
84602.m: With “3 for 2”, you get one third of the goods free.

84603.q: If you buy 10 or more exercise books, you get a 10 per cent discount. One exercise book costs 2.50 francs. How much do 12 exercise books cost?
84603.e: Without the discount, 12 exercise books cost 12 × 2.50 = 30 francs. With 10 per cent off, it is 30 minus 3 = 27 francs.
84603.m: A percentage discount is taken off the full price.

84604.q: A drink costs 1.20 francs on its own and a six-pack costs 6.00 francs. How much do you save per bottle with the six-pack?
84604.e: In the six-pack, one bottle costs 6.00 ÷ 6 = 1.00 franc. 1.20 minus 1.00 gives a saving of 0.20 francs.
84604.m: You get the price per item of a large pack by dividing by the number of items.

84605.q: A bike helmet costs 45 francs. If you buy several helmets, you get 20 per cent off each one. How much does one helmet cost then?
84605.e: 20 per cent of 45 francs is 9 francs. 45 minus 9 = 36 francs.
84605.m: After a 20 per cent discount, you still pay 80 per cent of the price.

84606.q: In a “buy 2, get 1 free” offer, a yoghurt costs 0.90 francs. How much do you pay for 6 yoghurts?
84606.e: Out of every 3 yoghurts, you only pay for 2. So for 6 yoghurts you pay 4 × 0.90 = 3.60 francs.
84606.m: With free-item offers, count how many items you actually pay for.

84607.q: One item costs 2 francs, but from 10 items upwards each one costs only 1.70 francs. How much do you pay for 10 items?
84607.e: From 10 items, the lower price applies to all of them: 10 × 1.70 = 17 francs. That is even less than 9 items at 18 francs.
84607.m: With tiered prices, a larger quantity can sometimes be cheaper overall.

84608.q: In a “second pack half price” offer, one pack costs 8 francs. What percentage discount do you get in total when you buy two packs?
84608.e: Two packs cost 8 + 4 = 12 instead of 16 francs. 4 ÷ 16 = 0.25, so 25 per cent.
84608.m: Half price on just one of two packs gives a quarter off overall.

84609.q: What do you take a digital photo with?
84609.e: A digital camera takes in light and saves the picture as a file. Mobile phones and tablets have a camera like this built in too.
84609.m: You take digital photos with a camera, including a phone camera.

84610.q: Unlike an old camera, what does a digital camera no longer need?
84610.e: Old cameras recorded the picture on film. A digital camera, on the other hand, saves the photo as a file.
84610.m: A digital camera saves photos as a file without film.

84611.q: What is the button on a camera that you press to take a photo called?
84611.e: When you press the shutter button, the camera takes the picture. On a phone the shutter button is often a round button on the screen.
84611.m: You take a photo with the shutter button.

84612.q: Through which part of the camera does the light come in?
84612.e: The lens is made of glass lenses. It directs the light into the inside of the camera.
84612.m: Light gets into the camera through the lens.

84613.q: What is the flash on a camera for?
a: It makes the photo more colourful
84613.e: When it is too dark, the flash lights up very briefly. That makes the photo brighter.
84613.m: The flash helps when it is too dark to take photos.

84614.q: You photograph a person with the sun shining brightly behind them. What does the person often look like in the photo?
84614.e: Bright light from behind is called backlight. The camera adjusts to the bright sun, so the person turns out dark.
84614.m: With backlight, the person in the photo is often too dark.

84615.q: What should you do before you send on a photo of another person?
84615.e: Everyone may decide for themselves where photos of them are shown. That is why you always ask first.
84615.m: I only show photos of others if they agree.

84616.q: What often happens if the camera wobbles while you take a photo?
84616.e: If the camera moves while taking the picture, the picture smudges. That is why you hold the camera still.
84616.m: If you hold the camera still, you get sharper photos.

84617.q: What do you do when you crop a photo?
84617.e: When cropping, you remove parts at the edge of the picture. That moves the important part to the centre.
84617.m: When cropping, you remove unimportant edges of a photo.

84618.q: A photo is much too dark. What do you turn up in the photo editor?
84618.e: With the brightness slider the whole picture gets brighter. Then you can see more again.
84618.m: You make photos that are too dark brighter with the brightness slider.

84619.q: A photo is upside down. What do you do in the photo editor?
84619.e: With the rotate function you can turn the picture a quarter turn or a half turn. Then it is the right way up.
84619.m: You can rotate crooked or upside-down photos in a photo editor.

84620.q: In a flash photo the eyes glow red. Which function helps?
84620.e: The flash reflects in the eye and makes it red. Red-eye correction turns those spots dark again.
84620.m: You can remove red eyes in flash photos with a special function.

84621.q: Which command undoes your last editing step?
84621.e: The Undo command takes back the last step. It often has an arrow symbol pointing to the left.
84621.m: With “Undo” you can take back a mistake straight away.

84622.q: Why is it best to save an edited photo as a copy?
84622.e: If you save as a copy, the unchanged photo is kept as well. That way you can start again later.
84622.m: If you save as a copy, you keep the original.

84623.q: What happens when you flip a photo in the photo editor?
84623.e: When you flip it, the picture looks as it would in a mirror. What was on the left before is on the right afterwards.
84623.m: When you flip a picture, its sides are swapped.

84624.q: What can you add to a photo in a photo editing app?
84624.e: Many apps let you put writing, stickers or frames on a photo. That way you can design an invitation, for example.
84624.m: In a photo editing app you can put text and stickers on photos.

84625.q: Which tool in a drawing program paints free lines like a real brush?
84625.e: With the brush you draw coloured lines wherever you move the mouse. You can set how thick it is.
84625.m: With the brush you paint free lines.

84626.q: Which tool fills a whole area with colour in one go?
84626.e: If you click with the paint bucket inside a closed area, the whole area is filled. If the area is not closed, the colour leaks out.
84626.m: With the paint bucket you fill areas in one click.

84627.q: Which tool do you use to remove something you have painted in a drawing program?
84627.e: The eraser deletes lines wherever you move over them. The background colour shows there again.
84627.m: The eraser removes painting in a drawing program.

84628.q: What do you usually draw with in a drawing program on a computer?
84628.e: With the mouse you move the pointer over the picture. If you hold the button down, it paints.
84628.m: On a computer you often draw with the mouse.

84629.q: What can you use to draw especially precisely on a tablet?
84629.e: A stylus has a tip that the screen recognises. With it you paint more precisely than with your finger.
84629.m: With a stylus you draw very precisely on a tablet.

84630.q: Where do you choose the colour in a drawing program?
84630.e: The colour palette shows lots of colour squares. Clicking one chooses the colour for the brush.
84630.m: In the colour palette you choose your painting colour.

84631.q: Which tool do you use to draw completely straight lines?
84631.e: With the line tool you set the start and end, and the program joins them in a straight line. Freehand this rarely works so precisely.
84631.m: For straight lines you use the line tool.

84632.q: What is the simple drawing program that has come with Windows for a long time called?
84632.e: Paint has been part of Windows since 1985. You can draw and edit simple pictures with it.
84632.m: Paint is a simple drawing program from Windows.

84633.q: What are pictures in pixel art made of?
84633.e: In pixel art you build the picture out of lots of small, clearly visible squares. Each square is a pixel.
